LETTER:
To the Road Authority

We are writing about the crossing outside our school at the Hill View Road site monitored by Crossing Watch.

In a 3.0 minute recording of 180.0 s we counted 8 pedestrian crossings and 10 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 32.2 km/h. Had a child been struck, the impact would almost certainly have been fatal. 3 of 8 crossings (1 in 2.7) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person; 2 of 8 (1 in 4) within 1.5 s. The exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 8.5-75.5% and 3.2-65.1% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

We recorded 2 serious near-misses defined as less than 1.5 s apart and 1 close pass defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart. A serious near-miss had a PET of 1.1 s with a motorcycle at 33.9 km/h.
For an adult hit by a car front at 33.9 km/h the estimated death risk is 2.1% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.
A 2nd serious near-miss had a PET of 0.0 s with a motorcycle at 16.6 km/h.
For an adult hit by a car front at 16.6 km/h the estimated death risk is 0.4% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.
A close pass had a PET of 1.5 s with a car at 24.7 km/h.
For an adult hit by a car front at 24.7 km/h the estimated death risk is 0.9% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.
At a 20 km/h limit the impact speeds would have been 5.9 km/h, 16.6 km/h and 6.5 km/h with adult death risks of 0.2%, 0.4% and 0.2% respectively.

PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 3.0 minutes. 73.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 gaps, 6 of them 12 s or more and longest 24.5 s, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to lower speeds and provide protected gaps.

We have the tracking data and can share the video file on request to assist your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the crossing outside our school at Canal Road crossing. Crossing Watch analysis of 34.6 minutes of video (2076.0 s) recorded 19 crossings and 23 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 56.5 km/h.

In that recording five of 19 crossings (1 in 3.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 1 of 19 (1 in 19) within 1.5 s. A close pass had a PET of 2.0 s with a van at 55.2 km/h.

A close pass had a PET of 2.1 s with a bus at 49.3 km/h.

A close pass had a PET of 2.3 s with a car at 32.6 km/h.

A close pass had a PET of 2.4 s with a van at 39.5 km/h.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 when scaled from 34.6 minutes, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can double-count by 1.3x. Also 93.8% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 8 gaps of 12 s or more and longest gap 53.8 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. We are not stating that any standard is met.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing to reduce approach speeds and give priority to pedestrians at this location.

We can share the video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the crossing outside our school at Canal Road crossing. Crossing Watch analysis of 34.6 minutes of video (2076.0 s) recorded 19 crossings and 23 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 56.5 km/h. A parent was injured here by a passing motorcycle earlier this year.

In that recording 5 of 19 crossings (1 in 3.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 1 of 19 (1 in 19) within 1.5 s. The 95% ranges if this recording is typical are 9.1-51.2% and 0.1-26.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.6-11.7 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

There was 1 serious near-miss and 4 close passes as defined by PET under 1.5 s and 1.5-3.0 s.

The serious near-miss had a PET of 0.9 s with a bus at 21.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk was 0.7%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.

A close pass had a PET of 2.0 s with a van at 55.2 km/h.

A close pass had a PET of 2.1 s with a bus at 49.3 km/h.

A close pass had a PET of 2.3 s with a car at 32.6 km/h.

A close pass had a PET of 2.4 s with a van at 39.5 km/h.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 when scaled from 34.6 minutes, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can double-count by 1.3x. Also 93.8% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 8 gaps of 12 s or more and longest gap 53.8 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. We are not stating that any standard is met.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing to reduce approach speeds and give priority to pedestrians at this location.

We can share the video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We would be pleased to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school on River Lane

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write to request a safer crossing outside our school.

We observed the crossing for 31.5 minutes and recorded 11 crossings and 8 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 49.9 km/h. There have already been injuries at this spot this school year.

We use the definition that a serious near-miss is a pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and a close pass is 1.5 to 3.0 s apart. In that period there were 0 serious near-misses and 1 close pass.

The worst event was a close pass with a gap of 2.7 s between pedestrian and vehicle. The vehicle involved was a car travelling at 47.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.0% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, based on 21 pedestrians and 15 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 31.5 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can overcount by 1.3x in our drone test. 45.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 7 gaps of 6 s or more including 1 gap of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 83.0 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and protect people crossing.

We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We are happy to share the video and underlying measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the crossing outside our school on Bridge Street.

A 3.8 minute recording (228.0 s) counted 10 pedestrian crossings and 24 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 28.8 km/h. In that time, 3 of 10 crossings (1 in 3.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 2 of 10 (1 in 5) within 1.5 s.

Another serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 18.0 km/h with a gap of 0.4 s. A close pass involved a bus at 17.1 km/h with a gap of 2.2 s. For an adult hit by a car front at 29.5 km/h the death risk is 1.4%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.

Assessment of PV² hourly rates needs at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 3.8 minutes. During the recording 80.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 7 gaps, 5 of them 12 s or more, longest 16.8 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing to slow traffic and protect people crossing.

We are happy to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at the Lantern Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school commissioned a video survey of the Lantern Road crossing. The recording lasted 2.1 minutes or 126.0 s and captured 7 pedestrian crossings and 25 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 52.3 km/h. The video showed 7 gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle.

In that recording, 6 of 7 crossings (1 in 1.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 4 of 7 (1 in 1.8) were within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 42.1-99.6% and 18.4-90.1% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson), and 2.2-13.1 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

By definition a serious near-miss is pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and a close pass is 1.5-3.0 s apart. There were 4 serious near-misses and 2 close passes.

The worst events recorded were:
One serious near-miss with pet of 1.0 s involved a van at 42.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 4.3% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared with 0.0% at a 20 km/h limit with impact at 0.0 km/h.
One serious near-miss with pet of 0.2 s involved a van at 36.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.7%, compared with 0.6% at a 20 km/h limit with impact at 20.0 km/h.
One serious near-miss with pet of 0.4 s involved an auto-rickshaw at 33.7 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.1%, compared with 0.6% at a 20 km/h limit with impact at 20.0 km/h.
One serious near-miss with pet of 0.5 s involved a van at 18.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.5%, compared with 0.5% at a 20 km/h limit with impact at 18.5 km/h.
One close pass with pet of 1.8 s involved a motorcycle at 44.6 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.6%, compared with 0.0% at a 20 km/h limit with impact at 0.0 km/h.

Engineering data are limited: PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 2.1 minutes, with 7 pedestrian crossings and 25 moving vehicles counted. 74.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 2 such gaps and 1 of them 12 s or more, longest 49.9 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. For reference UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds while other groups, such as children, may need 10-12 s or longer.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for pedestrians.

We are willing to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) for your review and will cooperate with any site inspection.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about safety at the Market Street crossing outside our school. A video survey of 39.9 minutes (2394.0 s) recorded 5 pedestrian crossings and 27 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 52.5 km/h.

The other serious near-miss was an auto-rickshaw at 12.9 km/h 0.7 s apart, with an adult death risk of 0.3%. The recording contained 2 gaps of at least 6 s and 1 gap of at least 12 s, the longest being 59.8 s.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location. We are happy to share the video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We are writing about pedestrian safety at the Mill Street crossing.

A 10.4 minute video (624.0 s) was analysed by Crossing Watch using SAM tracking and road-plane geometry. In that period 12 pedestrian crossings and 17 vehicles were counted, with an 85th percentile speed of 62.5 km/h. There were 7 gaps of 6 s or more, including 2 gaps of 12 s or more, and the longest gap was 43.1 s. In terms of engineering, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 10.4 minutes, and 41.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

During the observation there was 1 serious near-miss, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 5 close passes defined as 1.5 to 3.0 s apart. Of the interactions, 4 were person first, 2 were vehicle first and 0 were both at once.

The most serious event involved a bus at 13.9 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s.

For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.4%, from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+.

A separate close pass involved a motorcycle at 59.9 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 2.3 s.

For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.2%.

Another close pass involved a car at 33.6 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 2.2 s.

A further close pass involved a car at 41.4 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 2.6 s.

An additional close pass involved a van at 58.8 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 2.8 s.

To reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for people crossing, we request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements to support your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Station Road crossing

We measured activity at Station Road crossing for 36.0 minutes (2160.0 s). We recorded 5 crossings and 28 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 54.6 km/h. 4 of 5 crossings (1 in 1.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s of the person, and 2 of 5 (1 in 2.5) within 1.5 s.

One serious near-miss involved a bus at 53.3 km/h with 0.6 s between person and vehicle. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 10.9% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared with 0.5% if impact were at 17.3 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.

Another serious near-miss involved a van at 48.6 km/h with 0.6 s separation. For an adult the death risk would be 7.4%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h impact.

A close pass involved a car at 44.6 km/h with 2.4 s gap.

Another close pass involved a motorcycle at 21.9 km/h with 2.8 s gap. During 36.0 minutes there were 2 serious near-misses and 2 close passes.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 when scaled from 36.0 minutes to an hour, with the caveat that a formal count counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can count one person twice (1.3x in our drone test). 78.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 such gaps, 2 of them 12 s or more and longest 33.9 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce speeds and separate people and vehicles.

We can share the video and tracking data on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing on Hill View Road

Our school monitored the Hill View Road crossing for 20.1 minutes (1206.0 s). We counted 14 crossings and 23 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 51.9 km/h. Had a child been struck, the impact would almost certainly have been fatal. There was 1 gap of 6 s or more and 1 gap of 12 s or more, with the longest gap 49.4 s.

In that time there were 3 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s apart). In 2 cases the person was first, in 2 cases the vehicle was first, and in 1 case both were at once.

The worst incidents were as follows. 1 serious near-miss involved a van at 48.4 km/h with 1.0 s between road users; the adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 7.3% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). 1 serious near-miss involved a car at 21.8 km/h with 0.0 s between road users; the adult death risk is 0.7%. 1 serious near-miss involved a bus at 16.2 km/h with 0.9 s between road users; the adult death risk is 0.4%. 1 close pass involved a van at 47.8 km/h with 2.7 s between road users. 1 close pass involved a motorcycle at 26.6 km/h with 2.9 s between road users.

For engineering context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 42 pedestrians and 69 vehicles an hour scaled from 20.1 minutes of video, while a formal check counts the full peak hour. Also 95.1% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, from 1 such gap, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We can share the video for your review and welcome a site inspection.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority
Subject: Request for safety improvement at the Garden Road crossing

On the Garden Road crossing we recorded for 10.4 minutes (624.0 s) a total of 6 pedestrian crossings and 40 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 60.2 km/h. 6 gaps were cut short by the start or end of the video. In this period 6 of 6 crossings (1 in 1) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 5 of 6 (1 in 1.2) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 54.1-100.0% and 35.9-99.6% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 2.2-13.1 and 1.6-11.7 people in a recording this long (Poisson). Of the 5 serious near-misses and 1 close pass, 4 were person-first and 2 were vehicle-first as defined (serious: pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart; close pass: 1.5-3.0 s).

The worst near-misses illustrate the risk. One serious near-miss had a PET of 0.6 s with a van at 53.4 km/h; for an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 10.9% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared with 0.5% at an impact of 17.3 km/h if limited to 20 km/h. Another serious near-miss had a PET of 1.3 s with a car at 46.3 km/h; for an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 6.1%. A further serious near-miss had a PET of 0.2 s with a car at 44.1 km/h; for an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 5.1%. Another serious near-miss had a PET of 1.4 s with a car at 44.2 km/h; for an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 5.1%. Another serious near-miss had a PET of 0.8 s with an auto-rickshaw at 29.1 km/h; for an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 1.4%.

On engineering context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 10.4 minutes, with 6 pedestrian crossings and 40 moving vehicles. 88.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 2 gaps and 2 of them 12 s or more and longest 81.7 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. For reference, UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s as an acceptable gap at urban speeds and that other groups, such as children, may need 10-12 s or longer.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce approach speeds and provide priority for pedestrians.

We are willing to share the full video and Crossing Watch measurements with your engineers to assist assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We can share the video for your review and welcome a site inspection.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvements at Hill View Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning Hill View Road crossing outside our school.

Crossing Watch video measurements over 17.7 minutes recorded 27 crossings and 22 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 61.9 km/h. There were 11 gaps of 6 s or more and 2 gaps of 12 s or more, with the longest gap 37.6 s, and 87.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more. The observation used SAM tracking with road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time, where serious means pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass means 1.5 to 3.0 s.

In that period there was 1 serious near-miss and 3 close passes. Nearly all of the people seen crossing were unaccompanied schoolchildren. In 3 cases the person moved first and in 1 case the vehicle moved first, with 0 cases where both arrived at once. The most serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s and involved a car travelling at 31.9 km/h, with an adult death risk of 1.7% if hit by a car front, reducing to 0.6% at an impact speed of 20.0 km/h. A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.6 s and involved a van travelling at 56.0 km/h, with an adult death risk of 10.9% if hit. Another close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.1 s and involved an auto-rickshaw travelling at 24.6 km/h. A further close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.7 s and involved a car travelling at 19.4 km/h. All death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosén & Sander 2009.

For context, PV² was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8 based on 92 pedestrians and 75 moving vehicles per hour scaled from 17.7 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour. The gap share figure notes the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

We write about the Ring Road crossing outside our school and request a raised zebra crossing.

Measurements from video of the crossing, made by Crossing Watch with SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time, covered 33.8 minutes, 2028.0 s, with 29 crossings and 6 vehicles recorded.

The 85th percentile speed was 19.8 km/h. By these figures the crossing already qualifies for a signal-controlled crossing. There were 2 gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, 1 of them 12 s or more, with longest gap 86.4 s. In total 77.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more.

There was 1 serious near-miss and 0 close passes. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass as 1.5 to 3.0 s. In the serious case the vehicle arrived first in 1 case.

The worst serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 15.4 km/h. The pedestrian and the motorcycle were on the same spot 0.9 s apart. For an adult hit by a car front at that impact speed the death risk is 0.4% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts. At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 15.4 km/h with death risk 0.4% for an adult hit by a car front.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 51 pedestrians and 11 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 33.8 minutes of video. IRC:103-2012 cl. 6.7.4.1.2 notes a controlled crossing may be warranted above 1 x 10^8 on an undivided road and 2 x 10^8 on a divided road.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location and we offer to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Lantern Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school monitors the crossing outside our gate on Lantern Road. In 44.2 minutes of video (2652.0 s) we recorded 15 crossings and 25 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 39.7 km/h. The video showed 15 gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle.

By definition a serious near-miss is pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and a close pass is 1.5 s to 3.0 s. We recorded 2 serious near-misses and 2 close passes. In 3 cases the pedestrian entered first and in 1 case the vehicle entered first, with 0 cases where both were at the conflict point at once.

1 serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.9 s with a bus at 28.7 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 1.3% (0.6% at a 20.0 km/h limit with impact at 20.0 km/h) per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.

1 serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.0 s with a car at 21.1 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 0.7% (0.6% at a 20.0 km/h limit with impact at 20.0 km/h).

1 close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.7 s with a car at 35.9 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 1.5% (0.0% at a 20.0 km/h limit with impact at 0.0 km/h).

1 close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.5 s with a car at 16.6 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 0.4% (0.4% at a 20.0 km/h limit with impact at 16.6 km/h).

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 20 pedestrians and 34 moving vehicles per hour scaled from 44.2 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can count 1 person twice (1.3x the true count in our drone test).

66.3% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 5 gaps and 5 of them 12 s or more and longest 13.8 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video and that UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4 s to 6 s as an acceptable gap at urban speeds while other groups such as children may need 10 s to 12 s or longer.

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone signs at this location to reduce speeds and provide priority.

We offer to share the full video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We are writing about the crossing outside our school at Canal Road crossing.

In a recording lasting 126.0 s (2.1 minutes) we counted 3 pedestrian crossings and 14 moving vehicles. 3 of 3 crossings (1 in 1) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person; 3 of 3 (1 in 1) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 29.2-100.0% and 29.2-100.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson). We recorded 3 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. One near-miss involved a car at 44.2 km/h with a gap of 0.9 s. Another near-miss involved a van at 33.6 km/h with a gap of 0.1 s. A third near-miss involved a car at 19.1 km/h with a gap of 0.9 s. For adults hit by a car front (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), the death risk if hit was 5.1% at 44.2 km/h, 2.0% at 33.6 km/h and 0.6% at 19.1 km/h.

Engineering context is limited because PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 2.1 minutes. Counted: 3 pedestrian crossings, 14 moving vehicles. 79.8% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 3 gaps, 0 of them 12 s or more, longest 7.7 s (the first and last are cut short by the video).

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this crossing.

We would be happy to share the video and data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority
Subject: Request for safer crossing outside school on River Lane

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write regarding the River Lane crossing outside our school. Crossing Watch recorded 25 crossings in 36.0 minutes with 10 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 56.9 km/h. Once this fix is built, no one will die at this crossing.

In that period 2 of 25 crossings (1 in 12) were serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 of 25 (1 in 12) were within 3 s. Exact 95% ranges if this recording is typical are 1.0-26.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The most severe was a bus at 52.9 km/h passing 0.1 s after a person. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 10.6% from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.

The second serious near-miss was a van at 22.9 km/h passing 1.3 s after a person. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.8%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, scaled from 36.0 minutes of video while a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice. Also, 62.4% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 3 such gaps and longest 81.8 s, though the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for pupils crossing.

We have the video and tracking data and are happy to share them for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We are writing about the crossing at Quarry Road crossing following a 10.1 minute video survey lasting 606.0 s.

During that time we counted 11 pedestrian crossings and 42 moving vehicles with an 85th percentile speed of 54.5 km/h. A serious near miss is defined as a pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and a close pass is 1.5 to 3.0 s apart. We recorded 3 serious near misses and 3 close passes. For engineering context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 10.1 minutes, so they cannot be used here. 84.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 gaps of 6 s or more and 4 gaps of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 48.5 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video and that UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 13.5.2 states 4 to 6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds while other groups such as children may need 10 to 12 s or longer.

The worst events were as follows. One serious near miss involved a motorcycle at 52.9 km/h with 0.6 s between road users. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 10.5% based on Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+ and car fronts, compared with an impact speed of 17.7 km/h and death risk of 0.5% if the vehicle had been limited to 20 km/h.

A second serious near miss involved a bus at 37.6 km/h with 0.9 s between road users. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.9%, compared with an impact speed of 14.3 km/h and death risk of 0.4% at a 20 km/h limit.

A third serious near miss involved a car at 23.0 km/h with 0.3 s between road users. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.8%, compared with an impact speed of 20.0 km/h and death risk of 0.6% at a 20 km/h limit.

One close pass involved a car at 47.9 km/h with 1.5 s between road users. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 7.0%.

Another close pass involved a van at 43.4 km/h with 1.6 s between road users. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 3.8%.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce speeds and provide protected crossing priority. Most parents now avoid letting their children walk to school via this crossing.

We have the video and tracking data available and are happy to share them to support your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

A fourth serious near-miss had a PET of 0.0 s with a car at 22.4 km/h (adult death risk if hit by a car front 0.7%).

PV2 and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 11.7. 50.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 4 gaps, 1 of them 12 s or more, longest 54.9 s.

We would be pleased to share the video and counts to assist your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the crossing outside our school at Market Street crossing. Crossing Watch measured eight pedestrian crossings and 9 moving vehicles in 11.7 minutes (702.0 s).

5 of 8 crossings (1 in 1.6) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 4 of 8 (1 in 2) had a vehicle within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 24.5-91.5% and 15.7-84.3% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.6-11.7 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). The 85th percentile speed was 50.7 km/h. By definition serious is less than 1.5 s apart and close pass is 1.5-3.0 s.

One serious near-miss had a PET of 0.8 s with a motorcycle at 45.5 km/h (adult death risk if hit by a car front 5.7% per Rosen & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
Another serious near-miss had a PET of 0.3 s with a motorcycle at 40.0 km/h (adult death risk if hit by a car front 3.5%).
A third serious near-miss had a PET of 1.2 s with a car at 37.6 km/h (adult death risk if hit by a car front 2.9%).
A fourth serious near-miss had a PET of 0.0 s with a car at 22.4 km/h (adult death risk if hit by a car front 0.7%).
A close pass had a PET of 1.6 s with a bus at 50.1 km/h (adult death risk if hit by a car front 6.7%).

PV2 and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 11.7. 50.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 4 gaps, 1 of them 12 s or more, longest 54.9 s.

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and counts to assist your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Station Road crossing

We measured activity at Station Road crossing for 36.0 minutes (2160.0 s). We recorded 5 crossings and 28 vehicles. Many drivers were exceeding the posted speed limit as they passed through the crossing. The 85th percentile speed was 54.6 km/h. 4 of 5 crossings (1 in 1.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s of the person, and 2 of 5 (1 in 2.5) within 1.5 s.

Another serious near-miss involved a van at 48.6 km/h with 0.6 s separation. For an adult the death risk would be 7.4%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h impact.

A close pass involved a car at 44.6 km/h with 2.4 s gap.

Another close pass involved a motorcycle at 21.9 km/h with 2.8 s gap.

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce speeds and separate people and vehicles.

We can share the video and tracking data on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and counts to assist your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We are writing about the pedestrian crossing outside our school on River Lane. We arranged a Crossing Watch measurement of the crossing. In 7.0 minutes (420.0 s) it counted 11 pedestrian crossings and 10 moving vehicles, with an 85th-percentile speed of 54.4 km/h. By these figures the crossing already qualifies for a signal-controlled crossing. There were 3 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 close passes, defined as 1.5 s to 3.0 s apart. Where order could be seen, 4 interactions were person-first and 1 was vehicle-first.

The most severe near-miss was 0.3 s apart with a car at 49.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled adult death risk is 7.9%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A second serious near-miss was 1.2 s apart with a bus at 48.7 km/h, with a modelled adult death risk of 7.5% if hit.

A third serious near-miss was 1.2 s apart with a car at 45.7 km/h, with a modelled adult death risk of 5.8% if hit.

On engineering context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 7.0, so results are indicative only. 48.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 10 gaps, 0 of them 12 s or more, and the longest 8.8 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce approach speeds and give pedestrians clear priority.

We can share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements for your review and would welcome a site visit to discuss the design.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

Re: Safety of the pedestrian crossing on Cedar Lane

We write to request a raised zebra crossing outside our school.

Crossing Watch measurements over 4.7 minutes recorded 12 pedestrian crossings and 19 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 54.8 km/h. One near-miss ended with the vehicle hitting the person crossing.

2 serious near-misses and 4 close passes were recorded. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. Close pass is defined as 1.5 to 3.0 s apart.

One serious near-miss involved a bus at 40.3 km/h with a gap of 0.3 s. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 3.7%.

One serious near-miss involved a car at 35.1 km/h with a gap of 0.2 s. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 2.3%.

One close pass involved an auto-rickshaw at 50.2 km/h with a gap of 1.8 s.

One close pass involved a car at 34.6 km/h with a gap of 1.9 s.

One close pass involved a van at 21.9 km/h with a gap of 2.4 s.

All death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosen and Sander 2009.

Engineering context with caveats: PV2 and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 4.7 minutes. 61.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 7 gaps, 7 of them 12 s or more, longest 19.4 s, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We therefore request that you provide a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and protect children and adults crossing.

We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review and would welcome a site meeting.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning the Lantern Road crossing outside our school.

A video survey of 26.7 minutes (1602.0 s) recorded 40 crossings and 7 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 62.7 km/h. At its tightest, a vehicle and a person were on the same spot 0.7 s apart.

Another serious near-miss involved a van at 45.5 km/h with 0.1 s between road users.
Another serious near-miss involved a car at 34.8 km/h with 1.3 s between road users.
A further serious near-miss involved a bus at 15.8 km/h with 0.8 s between road users.
The close pass involved a car at 44.4 km/h with 1.9 s between road users.

For adults hit by a car front, Rosén & Sander 2009 gives death risk of 14.5% at 57.0 km/h, 5.7% at 45.5 km/h, 2.3% at 34.8 km/h, 0.4% at 15.8 km/h and 1.9% at 44.4 km/h.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, based on 90 pedestrians and 16 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 26.7 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice at 1.3x the true count in drone tests.
63.2% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, from 12 gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 73.9 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write to request a safety improvement at the crossing outside our school. We commissioned a Crossing Watch measurement using SAM tracking and road-plane geometry to assess post-encroachment time.

Over 11.1 minutes (666.0 s) the video counted twelve pedestrian crossings and 11 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 48.4 km/h. In that period 4 of 12 crossings (1 in 3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 3 of 12 crossings (1 in 4) were within 1.5 s.

The video found 3 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart. The worst serious near-miss was 1.2 s apart involving an auto-rickshaw at 47.4 km/h. A second serious near-miss was 0.2 s apart involving a van at 44.0 km/h. A third serious near-miss was 0.4 s apart involving an auto-rickshaw at 13.1 km/h. The close pass was 1.9 s apart involving a car at 50.1 km/h.
For adults hit by a car front, Rosén and Sander 2009 gives an adult death risk if hit of 6.7% for the 47.4 km/h case, 5.0% for the 44.0 km/h case, 0.3% for the 13.1 km/h case, and 3.2% for the 50.1 km/h case. For context, PV2 and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 11.1 minutes. The recording also shows 66.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 such gaps and 3 of them 12 s or more and a longest gap of 33.6 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h markings at this location.

We are willing to share the video and measurement files for your review.

Yours faithfully,

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing outside the school on Lake View Road

We write regarding the crossing outside our school on Lake View Road. A Crossing Watch review of 21.4 minutes of video (1284.0 s) recorded 11 crossings and 22 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 50.9 km/h. A young pupil hit by the fastest vehicle would probably not have survived.

The review found 4 of 11 crossings (1 in 2.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 3 of 11 (1 in 3.7) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 10.9-69.2% and 6.0-61.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There were 3 serious near-misses and 1 close pass as defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 1.5-3.0 s respectively.

The worst near-misses were:
One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s with a car at 51.3 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 9.2% from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.7 s with an auto-rickshaw at 42.7 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 4.5%, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s with an auto-rickshaw at 37.7 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 2.9%, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
One close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.7 s with a car at 51.5 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 6.1%.

In engineering terms, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 31 pedestrians and 62 moving vehicles an hour, scaled from 21.4 minutes of video, and a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice as 1.3x the true count in our drone test. Also 43.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 3 gaps and 1 of them 12 s or more and longest 17.6 s, with the caveat that the first and last are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide a protected crossing.

We are willing to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We write concerning the Brook Street crossing outside our school. A 6.2 minute video recording (372.0 s) counted 9 pedestrian crossings and 29 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 62.5 km/h.

Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 13.7-78.8% and 2.8-60.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

A further close pass involved a car at 25.7 km/h with a gap of 1.8 s. The adult death risk if hit at that speed is 0.4%.

For context on gaps, 41.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 12 gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 58.1 s (the first and last are cut short by the video). PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 6.2. Counted: 9 pedestrian crossings, 29 moving vehicles.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for pupils crossing.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

The worst near-misses were:
One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s with a car at 51.3 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 9.2% from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.7 s with an auto-rickshaw at 42.7 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 4.5%, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s with an auto-rickshaw at 37.7 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 2.9%, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
One close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.7 s with a car at 51.5 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 6.1%.

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing outside the school on Lake View Road

We write regarding the crossing outside our school on Lake View Road. A Crossing Watch review of 21.4 minutes of video (1284.0 s) recorded 11 crossings and 22 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 50.9 km/h. Many of these drivers were not watching the road at all.

The review found 4 of 11 crossings (1 in 2.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 3 of 11 (1 in 3.7) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 10.9-69.2% and 6.0-61.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There were 3 serious near-misses and 1 close pass as defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 1.5-3.0 s respectively.

The worst near-misses were:
One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s with a car at 51.3 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 9.2% from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.7 s with an auto-rickshaw at 42.7 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 4.5%, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s with an auto-rickshaw at 37.7 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 2.9%, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
One close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.7 s with a car at 51.5 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 6.1%.

In engineering terms, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 31 pedestrians and 62 moving vehicles an hour, scaled from 21.4 minutes of video, and a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice as 1.3x the true count in our drone test. Also 43.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 3 gaps and 1 of them 12 s or more and longest 17.6 s, with the caveat that the first and last are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide a protected crossing.

We are willing to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
Approved by The Principal for issue

One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.2 s with a car travelling at 32.9 km/h. Adult death risk if hit at that speed is 1.9%, falling to 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.
One close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.8 s with a car travelling at 56.4 km/h. Adult death risk if hit at that speed is 7.2%.

PV2 was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 127 pedestrians and 22 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 16.6 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour.

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table to reduce vehicle speeds toward 20 km/h where adult death risk is lower. We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing outside the school on Lake View Road

We write regarding the crossing outside our school on Lake View Road. A Crossing Watch review of 21.4 minutes of video (1284.0 s) recorded 11 crossings and 22 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 50.9 km/h. Among the worst near-misses measured, the fastest vehicle was going at 51.5 km/h.

The review found 4 of 11 crossings (1 in 2.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 3 of 11 (1 in 3.7) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 10.9-69.2% and 6.0-61.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There were 3 serious near-misses and 1 close pass as defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 1.5-3.0 s respectively.

The worst near-misses were:
One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s with a car at 51.3 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 9.2% from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.7 s with an auto-rickshaw at 42.7 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 4.5%, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s with an auto-rickshaw at 37.7 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 2.9%, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
One close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.7 s with a car at 51.5 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 6.1%.

In engineering terms, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 31 pedestrians and 62 moving vehicles an hour, scaled from 21.4 minutes of video, and a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice as 1.3x the true count in our drone test. Also 43.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 3 gaps and 1 of them 12 s or more and longest 17.6 s, with the caveat that the first and last are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide a protected crossing.

We are willing to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
Approved by The Principal for issue

Dear Road Authority Manager,

We are writing about safety at the Brook Street crossing outside our school. A Crossing Watch analysis of video covering 8.8 minutes (528.0 s) counted 12 pedestrian crossings and 17 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 59.0 km/h. There were 3 serious near-misses defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 0 close passes of 1.5 s to 3.0 s. In all 3 serious cases the vehicle was first.

One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.3 s with a car at 58.6 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 16.5% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+).

A second serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.8 s with a car at 58.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 16.0%.

A third serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.0 s with a car at 20.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.6%.

At a 20 km/h limit the modelled impact speed would be 0.0 km/h with 0.0% adult death risk for the first 2 events and 20.0 km/h with 0.6% adult death risk for the third event.

Engineering context is limited: PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 8.8 minutes. The data show 96.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 10 such gaps including 4 of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 43.8 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4 s to 6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds and other groups, such as children, may need 10 s to 12 s or longer.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing to reduce vehicle speeds and provide a protected crossing point.

We can share the video for your review on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing outside the school on Lake View Road

We write regarding the crossing outside our school on Lake View Road. A Crossing Watch review of 21.4 minutes of video (1284.0 s) recorded 11 crossings and 22 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 50.9 km/h. The death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

The review found 4 of 11 crossings (1 in 2.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 3 of 11 (1 in 3.7) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 10.9-69.2% and 6.0-61.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There were 3 serious near-misses and 1 close pass as defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 1.5-3.0 s respectively.

The worst near-misses were:
One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s with a car at 51.3 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 9.2% from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.7 s with an auto-rickshaw at 42.7 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 4.5%, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s with an auto-rickshaw at 37.7 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 2.9%, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
One close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.7 s with a car at 51.5 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 6.1%.

In engineering terms, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 31 pedestrians and 62 moving vehicles an hour, scaled from 21.4 minutes of video, and a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice as 1.3x the true count in our drone test. Also 43.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 3 gaps and 1 of them 12 s or more and longest 17.6 s, with the caveat that the first and last are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide a protected crossing.

We are willing to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority
Subject: Request for safety improvement at the Garden Road crossing

On the Garden Road crossing we recorded for 10.4 minutes (624.0 s) a total of 6 pedestrian crossings and 40 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 60.2 km/h. In the near-miss with a time gap of 0.6 s the vehicle was going at 46.3 km/h, and in the one with a time gap of 1.3 s it was going at 53.4 km/h. In this period 6 of 6 crossings (1 in 1) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 5 of 6 (1 in 1.2) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 54.1-100.0% and 35.9-99.6% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 2.2-13.1 and 1.6-11.7 people in a recording this long (Poisson). Of the 5 serious near-misses and 1 close pass, 4 were person-first and 2 were vehicle-first as defined (serious: pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart; close pass: 1.5-3.0 s).

The worst near-misses illustrate the risk. One serious near-miss had a PET of 0.6 s with a van at 53.4 km/h; for an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 10.9% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared with 0.5% at an impact of 17.3 km/h if limited to 20 km/h. Another serious near-miss had a PET of 1.3 s with a car at 46.3 km/h; for an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 6.1%. A further serious near-miss had a PET of 0.2 s with a car at 44.1 km/h; for an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 5.1%. Another serious near-miss had a PET of 1.4 s with a car at 44.2 km/h; for an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 5.1%. Another serious near-miss had a PET of 0.8 s with an auto-rickshaw at 29.1 km/h; for an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 1.4%.

On engineering context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 10.4 minutes, with 6 pedestrian crossings and 40 moving vehicles. 88.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 2 gaps and 2 of them 12 s or more and longest 81.7 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. For reference, UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s as an acceptable gap at urban speeds and that other groups, such as children, may need 10-12 s or longer.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce approach speeds and provide priority for pedestrians.

We are willing to share the full video and Crossing Watch measurements with your engineers to assist assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school

We measured activity at the crossing outside the school for 40.6 minutes (2436.0 s). In that time we recorded 22 crossings and 29 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 41.9 km/h. The drivers involved were speeding because they were late for work.

Of the 22 crossings, 4 (1 in 5.5) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s of the person, and 1 of 22 (1 in 22) was within 1.5 s. We class serious as less than 1.5 s apart and close pass as 1.5-3.0 s. There was 1 serious near-miss and 3 close passes.

The most serious was a car at 40.2 km/h passing 1.0 s after the person. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 3.6% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A second event was a motorcycle at 31.3 km/h with a gap of 2.5 s.

A third event was a van at 42.5 km/h with a gap of 2.5 s.

A fourth event was a car at 23.0 km/h with a gap of 2.9 s.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 when scaled as 33 pedestrians and 43 moving vehicles an hour from 40.6 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour. 67.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 4 such gaps including 1 of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 60.8 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We can share the video and tracking data on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school

We measured activity at the crossing outside the school for 40.6 minutes (2436.0 s). In that time we recorded 22 crossings and 29 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 41.9 km/h. Near-misses like these occur every morning when school opens.

Of the 22 crossings, 4 (1 in 5.5) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s of the person, and 1 of 22 (1 in 22) was within 1.5 s. We class serious as less than 1.5 s apart and close pass as 1.5-3.0 s. There was 1 serious near-miss and 3 close passes.

The most serious was a car at 40.2 km/h passing 1.0 s after the person. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 3.6% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A second event was a motorcycle at 31.3 km/h with a gap of 2.5 s.

A third event was a van at 42.5 km/h with a gap of 2.5 s.

A fourth event was a car at 23.0 km/h with a gap of 2.9 s.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 when scaled as 33 pedestrians and 43 moving vehicles an hour from 40.6 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour. 67.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 4 such gaps including 1 of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 60.8 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We can share the video and tracking data on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority regarding Canal Road crossing. Dear Sir/Madam, In 7.3 minutes (438.0 s) of video, Crossing Watch recorded 7 pedestrian crossings and 26 vehicles. 5 of 7 crossings (1 in 1.4) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s of the person, and 4 of 7 (1 in 1.8) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 29.0-96.3% and 18.4-90.1% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.6-11.7 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). Of the 5 near-misses, 4 were serious (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 1 was a close pass (1.5-3.0 s). 3 were person-first and 2 were vehicle-first. One serious near-miss had a PET of 0.2 s with a car at 57.3 km/h, with an adult death risk of 14.9% if hit (0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h). All of the pedestrians involved were children on their way home. Another serious near-miss had a PET of 0.4 s with a motorcycle at 56.2 km/h, with an adult death risk of 13.7% if hit (0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h). Another serious near-miss had a PET of 0.1 s with a car at 52.6 km/h, with an adult death risk of 10.3% if hit (0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h). Another serious near-miss had a PET of 0.7 s with a bus at 21.6 km/h, with an adult death risk of 0.7% if hit (0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h). One close pass had a PET of 2.5 s with a car at 47.5 km/h. Death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, with no child risk stated. The 85th percentile speed was 64.3 km/h. Engineering context is limited: PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 7.3, with 7 pedestrian crossings and 26 moving vehicles counted. 52.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 9 gaps, 5 of them 12 s or more, longest 13.8 s, noting the first and last are cut short by the video. We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h markings at this location. We are willing to share the video and SAM tracking data for your review. Yours faithfully, The Principal Approved by The Principal on file review

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the crossing at Quarry Road crossing outside our school.

We arranged a video survey for 8.1 minutes (486.0 s). In that time 11 pedestrian crossings and 19 moving vehicles were counted. The 85th percentile speed was 54.3 km/h during the 8.1 minutes. There were 4 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart.

One serious near-miss involved a bus at 55.9 km/h with 0.5 s between road users. For an adult hit by a car front at 55.9 km/h the death risk would be 13.4%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.

A second serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 54.1 km/h with 0.0 s between road users. For an adult hit by a car front at 54.1 km/h the death risk would be 11.6%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.

A third serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 43.0 km/h with 0.0 s between road users. For an adult hit by a car front at 43.0 km/h the death risk would be 4.6%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.

A fourth serious near-miss involved a car at 13.9 km/h with 0.1 s between road users. For an adult hit by a car front at 13.9 km/h the death risk would be 0.4%, compared with 0.4% at an impact of 13.9 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.

We note PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 8.1 minutes, so counts are indicative only. Also 94.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with 10 gaps, longest 71.4 s, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this crossing to slow traffic and give priority to pedestrians.

We are happy to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We measured activity at the crossing outside the school for 40.6 minutes (2436.0 s). In that time we recorded 22 crossings and 29 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 41.9 km/h. Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority
Subject: Request for safety improvement at the Garden Road crossing

On the Garden Road crossing we recorded for 10.4 minutes (624.0 s) a total of 6 pedestrian crossings and 40 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 60.2 km/h. In this period 6 of 6 crossings (1 in 1) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 5 of 6 (1 in 1.2) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 54.1-100.0% and 35.9-99.6% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 2.2-13.1 and 1.6-11.7 people in a recording this long (Poisson). Of the 5 serious near-misses and 1 close pass, 4 were person-first and 2 were vehicle-first as defined (serious: pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart; close pass: 1.5-3.0 s).

The worst near-misses illustrate the risk. One serious near-miss had a PET of 0.6 s with a van at 53.4 km/h; for an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 10.9% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared with 0.5% at an impact of 17.3 km/h if limited to 20 km/h. Another serious near-miss had a PET of 1.3 s with a car at 46.3 km/h; for an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 6.1%. A further serious near-miss had a PET of 0.2 s with a car at 44.1 km/h; for an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 5.1%. Another serious near-miss had a PET of 1.4 s with a car at 44.2 km/h; for an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 5.1%. Another serious near-miss had a PET of 0.8 s with an auto-rickshaw at 29.1 km/h; for an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 1.4%.

On engineering context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 10.4 minutes, with 6 pedestrian crossings and 40 moving vehicles. 88.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 2 gaps and 2 of them 12 s or more and longest 81.7 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. For reference, UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s as an acceptable gap at urban speeds and that other groups, such as children, may need 10-12 s or longer.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce approach speeds and provide priority for pedestrians.

We are willing to share the full video and Crossing Watch measurements with your engineers to assist assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

A further close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.4 s and involved a car at 24.6 km/h.

Also, 67.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 8 gaps and 7 of them 12 s or more and longest gap 33.8 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you provide a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this crossing to reduce vehicle speeds and to give pedestrians priority.

We are happy to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements to assist your assessment.

Yours faithfully,

The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Brook Street crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school asked Crossing Watch to video the Brook Street crossing. In 38.3 minutes of video (2298.0 s) there were 8 pedestrian crossings and 29 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 48.7 km/h. Over half of the vehicles observed were exceeding the posted speed limit. There were 2 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 close passes (1.5 to 3.0 s apart). In 3 cases the pedestrian was first and in 1 case the vehicle was first.

The worst incidents were:
One serious near-miss had a gap of 0.9 s with a bus at 49.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death-risk estimate from Rosén & Sander 2009 is 7.7%.
One serious near-miss had a gap of 1.2 s with a car at 37.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death-risk estimate from Rosén & Sander 2009 is 2.9%.
One close pass had a gap of 2.1 s with a van at 31.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death-risk estimate from Rosén & Sander 2009 is 0.2%.
One close pass had a gap of 2.6 s with an auto-rickshaw at 48.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front the death-risk estimate from Rosén & Sander 2009 is given as 0.0% for this case.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, calculated as 13 pedestrians and 45 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 38.3 minutes of video, while a formal check counts the full peak hour. Also 82.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 5 gaps and 5 of them 12 s or more and longest 59.5 s, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce speeds and give pedestrians priority. We are willing to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

I write concerning the North Avenue crossing outside our school.

A Crossing Watch review of 11.5 minutes (690.0 s) recorded 12 pedestrian crossings and 21 moving vehicles.
The 85th percentile speed was 46.9 km/h. A young pupil hit by the fastest vehicle would probably not have survived.

In 4 interactions the vehicle went first, in 0 the person went first, and in 1 both were there at once.

A car at 25.1 km/h was 0.0 s apart from a pedestrian. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the published death risk is 1.0%.
A bus at 20.8 km/h was 1.2 s apart from a pedestrian. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the published death risk is 0.6%.
At a 20.0 km/h impact speed the published adult death risk would be 0.6%.

72.8% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 2 gaps of 6 s or more and 0 of 12 s or more and longest gap 8.9 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this crossing to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for pedestrians.

We can share the video and tracking data on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir or Madam,

Re: Safety at Brook Street crossing

We write on behalf of our school about the crossing outside it. A video survey of 7.3 minutes (438.0 s) recorded 3 pedestrian crossings and 6 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 57.4 km/h.

Of 3 crossings, 3 had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s, and 0 of 3 within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges if this recording is typical are 29.2-100.0% and 0.0-70.8% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.0-3.7 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

There were 0 serious near-misses by the definition of pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 3 close passes of 1.5-3.0 s.

The closest pass was a close pass with PET of 1.7 s involving a car at 51.0 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 5.8% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
Another close pass had a PET of 1.6 s involving a motorcycle at 31.9 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 1.4%. A child struck in this type of collision would have faced a 12% chance of dying.
A third close pass had a PET of 1.8 s involving a bus at 21.9 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 0.3%.

For context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 7.3 minutes with 3 crossings and 6 moving vehicles, so rates from this short sample must be treated with caution. In this sample 96.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 such gaps and 5 of 12 s or more and longest 75.0 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and give pedestrians priority.

We have the Crossing Watch video and tracking data using SAM road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time and are happy to share it.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Garden Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We asked Crossing Watch to survey the Garden Road crossing. In 39.2 minutes of video 13 crossings and 30 vehicles were recorded, with an 85th percentile speed of 41.9 km/h. The closest near-miss measured had a time gap of 1.4 s.
There were 2 serious near-misses and 3 close passes. Serious means less than 1.5 s between pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot, close pass means 1.5 to 3.0 s. In 3 cases the person was first, in 2 the vehicle was first.
One serious near-miss involved a van at 34.5 km/h with a gap of 0.7 s, carrying an adult death risk of 2.2% if hit by a car front, which would be 0.6% at an impact speed of 20.0 km/h.
A second serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 30.8 km/h with a gap of 1.4 s, carrying an adult death risk of 1.6%.
A close pass involved a van at 38.1 km/h with a gap of 1.8 s, carrying an adult death risk of 1.4%.
A close pass involved a car at 32.6 km/h with a gap of 1.7 s, carrying an adult death risk of 1.1%.
A close pass involved an auto-rickshaw at 35.5 km/h with a gap of 1.8 s, carrying an adult death risk of 1.1%. Death-risk figures are from Rosen & Sander 2009 for adults aged 15 and over hit by a car front.
Engineering review notes PV2 was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8 from 20 pedestrians and 46 vehicles an hour scaled from 39.2 minutes of video, whereas a formal check counts the full peak hour. 43.0% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 5 such gaps and 2 of 12 s or more and the longest 68.6 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.
We request a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for people crossing. We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the crossing outside our school on Mill Street.

Measurements from 44.3 minutes of video recorded 35 crossings and 22 vehicles. 4 of 35 crossings (1 in 8.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 2 of 35 (1 in 18) were within 1.5 s. There were 2 serious near-misses and 2 close passes. One serious near-miss involved a van at 52.0 km/h with a gap of 1.2 s. Another serious near-miss involved a car at 18.4 km/h with a gap of 0.9 s. We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce speeds and protect people crossing.

We would be happy to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning the crossing on Brook Street (Brook Street crossing). Crossing Watch measurements from 7.9 minutes of video counted 11 pedestrian crossings and 34 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 54.6 km/h.

In that period we recorded 3 serious near-misses and 2 close passes. Serious means pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, close pass means 1.5-3.0 s apart.

One serious near-miss had a gap of 1.1 s with a bus travelling at 46.9 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 6.4% for an adult hit by a car front.
Another serious near-miss had a gap of 1.2 s with a bus travelling at 42.6 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 4.4% for an adult hit by a car front.
A third serious near-miss had a gap of 0.6 s with a van travelling at 38.1 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 3.0% for an adult hit by a car front.
One close pass had a gap of 2.0 s with a car travelling at 53.4 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 3.2% for an adult hit by a car front.
Another close pass had a gap of 2.4 s with a motorcycle travelling at 13.9 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 0.0% for an adult hit by a car front.
Risk figures are from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by car fronts.

For context on gaps, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 7.9 minutes. 83.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 2 such gaps and 0 of them 12 s or more and a longest gap of 10.7 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with a speed table to slow approaching traffic and give pedestrians priority.

We would be pleased to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
Approved by The Principal
