LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Canal Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

On behalf of the school I write to request a raised zebra crossing on a speed table with 20 km/h signs and markings at Canal Road crossing. Once this fix is built, no one will die at this crossing.

A 5.4 minute video survey (324.0 s) recorded 12 pedestrian crossings and 28 moving vehicles.

The 85th percentile speed was 50.2 km/h.

In the recording 5 of 12 crossings (1 in 2.4) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person.

In the recording 2 of 12 crossings (1 in 6) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 1.5 s of the person.

We write about the School Lane crossing on behalf of the school. Crossing Watch video recorded 9.8 minutes (588.0 s) with 3 pedestrian crossings and 7 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 45.2 km/h.

In that recording, 1 of 3 crossings (1 in 3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person; 0 of 3 within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical: 0.8-90.6% and 0.0-70.8% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson); 0.0-5.6 and 0.0-3.7 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There were 0 serious near-misses and 1 close pass. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart; close pass is 1.5-3.0 s.

The worst event was a close pass with a post-encroachment time of 2.6 s involving a car. The car was travelling at 39.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.0% per Rosen & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts. This pattern proves that pupils face a severe risk of fatal injury at this crossing every school day.

For context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 9.8. 54.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 7 gaps, 4 of them 12 s or more, longest 19.9 s (the first and last are cut short by the video).

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with 20 km/h zone and signage to reduce speeds and provide protected priority for pupils.

We are happy to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

Re: Safety request for Quarry Road crossing

We write to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table outside our school.

Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) measured the crossing for 9.0 minutes (540.0 s) and counted 5 pedestrian crossings and 6 vehicles. During 9.0 minutes there were 5 crossings and 6 vehicles with 8 gaps lasting 6 s. The 85th percentile speed was 58.1 km/h.

In that period there was 1 serious near-miss (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s). Person-first was 2 and vehicle-first was 1.

The most serious event had a PET of 0.4 s and involved a bus at 49.3 km/h. An adult hit by a car front at that speed would have a death risk of 7.8%, falling to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A second event had a PET of 1.9 s and involved a van at 56.5 km/h. An adult hit by a car front at that speed would have a death risk of 5.6%.

A third event had a PET of 2.0 s and involved a motorcycle at 30.0 km/h. An adult hit by a car front at that speed would have a death risk of 0.3%.

PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 9.0. We also note that 52.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed. There were 8 gaps of 6 s and 1 gap of 12 s, longest 66.2 s, but the first and last are cut short by the video.

We ask the authority to install the raised zebra crossing with speed table noted above to reduce speeds and protect pedestrians. We are happy to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at River Lane crossing

We write regarding the River Lane crossing outside our school. Crossing Watch recorded 35 crossings and 6 moving vehicles in 16.6 minutes (996.0 s) of video using SAM tracking and road-plane geometry.

6 of 35 crossings (1 in 5.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person; 2 of 35 (1 in 18) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical: 6.6-33.6% and 0.7-19.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson); 2.2-13.1 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

There were 2 serious near-misses (post-encroachment time less than 1.5 s) and 4 close passes (1.5-3.0 s).
One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.6 s with an auto-rickshaw travelling at 33.8 km/h. Adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 2.1% per Rosen & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts, falling to 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.
One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.2 s with a car travelling at 32.9 km/h. Adult death risk if hit at that speed is 1.9%, falling to 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.
One close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.8 s with a car travelling at 56.4 km/h. Adult death risk if hit at that speed is 7.2%.

The 85th percentile speed was 54.6 km/h. In 16.6 minutes, 3 crossings had the person arrive first and 3 had the vehicle arrive first.
67.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 4 gaps, 2 of them 12 s or more, longest 54.8 s. The first and last are cut short by the video.
PV2 was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 127 pedestrians and 22 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 16.6 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour.

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table to reduce vehicle speeds toward 20 km/h where adult death risk is lower. We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

I write on behalf of our school regarding the crossing outside our premises at Park Avenue crossing.

We commissioned a video survey of 35.3 minutes, which is 2118.0 s. In that time 3 crossings and 4 vehicles were observed. The 85th percentile speed was 23.9 km/h.

The survey recorded 1 serious near-miss, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. The worst case had a post-encroachment time of 0.7 s and involved an auto-rickshaw travelling at 22.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.8 percent. At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 20.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.6 percent for an adult, based on Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15 plus, car fronts.

For context, PV² was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8 from 5 pedestrians and 7 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 35.3 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour. Also, 74.1 percent of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location. Many pupils dash across Park Avenue each morning because drivers ignore the crossing.

We would be pleased to share the video and data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety works at Bridge Street crossing

We write from the school beside Bridge Street crossing. Crossing Watch measured the crossing for 25.8 minutes and recorded 32 crossings and 15 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 47.4 km/h.

In 25.8 minutes the video logged 32 crossings, 15 vehicles and 1 serious near-miss with a 0.3 s gap involving a bus at 46.0 km/h. The close pass involved a bus at 22.2 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 1.7 s.

For adults hit by a car front, Rosén & Sander 2009 estimates the death risk at 46.0 km/h as 5.9% and at 22.2 km/h as 0.4%. At a 20.0 km/h limit the estimated impact speed for the worst case would be 20.0 km/h with 0.6% adult death risk, and for the second case 2.5 km/h with 0.1% adult death risk.

We request a raised zebra crossing on a speed table with 20 km/h zone signs and markings at this location. We will share the full video and data on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

The review found 4 serious near-misses and 1 close pass. Serious means pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. Close pass means 1.5-3.0 s.

Counts were 2 with person first and 3 with vehicle first and 0 with both at once.

The bus serious encounter had a gap of 0.3 s. The bus speed was 55.3 km/h with adult death risk if hit of 12.8 % for car fronts. At 20.0 km/h the modelled impact was 20.0 km/h with adult death risk of 0.6 %.

The car serious encounter had a gap of 0.3 s. The car speed was 48.0 km/h with adult death risk if hit of 7.0 % for car fronts. At 20.0 km/h the modelled impact was 20.0 km/h with adult death risk of 0.6 %.

The car serious encounter had a gap of 1.1 s. The car speed was 39.1 km/h with adult death risk if hit of 3.3 % for car fronts. At 20.0 km/h the modelled impact was 0.0 km/h with adult death risk of 0.0 %.

The van serious encounter had a gap of 0.9 s. The van speed was 36.1 km/h with adult death risk if hit of 2.5 % for car fronts. At 20.0 km/h the modelled impact was 16.5 km/h with adult death risk of 0.4 %.

The van close pass encounter had a gap of 1.6 s. The van speed was 25.2 km/h with adult death risk if hit of 0.8 % for car fronts. At 20.0 km/h the modelled impact was 0.0 km/h with adult death risk of 0.0 %.

On engineering, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video while this video is 8.8. In this video 62.3 % of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing at this location to slow traffic and give priority to crossing pupils.

We offer to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

Subject: Request to make the Ring Road crossing safer

Measurements were made from video of the crossing by Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time). In 16.1 minutes (966.0 s) we recorded 14 crossings and 37 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 48.5 km/h.

We recorded 3 serious near-misses and 3 close passes. Many pupils cross here unaccompanied on their way to school each morning. Serious means pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. Close pass means 1.5 s to 3.0 s apart.

The worst events were:
One serious near-miss had a PET of 0.3 s with a car travelling at 46.3 km/h. For an adult hit at that speed by a car front the estimated death risk is 6.1%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.
Another serious near-miss had a PET of 0.0 s with a car travelling at 35.0 km/h. For an adult hit at that speed by a car front the estimated death risk is 2.3%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.
A 3rd serious near-miss had a PET of 0.6 s with a car travelling at 28.9 km/h. For an adult hit at that speed by a car front the estimated death risk is 1.3%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.
Death-risk figures are Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.

For context, scaled PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 52 pedestrians and 138 moving vehicles per hour scaled from 16.1 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count 1 person twice (1.3x the true count in our drone test).
Also 61.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 1 gap of 6 s or more, longest 82.0 s, with the caveat that the 1st and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and the full measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Road Authority,

The school arranged Crossing Watch tracking at Garden Road crossing. In 8.8 minutes of video there were 6 pedestrian crossings and 12 moving vehicles with 85th percentile speed of 55.3 km/h.

The review found 4 serious near-misses and 1 close pass. Serious means pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. Close pass means 1.5-3.0 s.

Counts were 2 with person first and 3 with vehicle first and 0 with both at once.

The bus serious encounter had a gap of 0.3 s. The bus speed was 55.3 km/h with adult death risk if hit of 12.8 % for car fronts. At 20.0 km/h the modelled impact was 20.0 km/h with adult death risk of 0.6 %.

The car serious encounter had a gap of 0.3 s. The car speed was 48.0 km/h with adult death risk if hit of 7.0 % for car fronts. At 20.0 km/h the modelled impact was 20.0 km/h with adult death risk of 0.6 %.

The car serious encounter had a gap of 1.1 s. The car speed was 39.1 km/h with adult death risk if hit of 3.3 % for car fronts. At 20.0 km/h the modelled impact was 0.0 km/h with adult death risk of 0.0 %.

The van serious encounter had a gap of 0.9 s. The van speed was 36.1 km/h with adult death risk if hit of 2.5 % for car fronts. At 20.0 km/h the modelled impact was 16.5 km/h with adult death risk of 0.4 %.

The van close pass encounter had a gap of 1.6 s. The van speed was 25.2 km/h with adult death risk if hit of 0.8 % for car fronts. At 20.0 km/h the modelled impact was 0.0 km/h with adult death risk of 0.0 %.

Risk figures are from Rosén and Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.

On engineering, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video while this video is 8.8. In this video 62.3 % of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing at this location to slow traffic and give priority to crossing pupils.

We offer to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning the Canal Road crossing outside our school. We commissioned a Crossing Watch analysis using SAM tracking and road-plane geometry with post-encroachment time, where serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass is 1.5-3.0 s.

In 9.9 minutes of video, which is 594.0 s, we counted 9 pedestrian crossings and 5 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 50.1 km/h. The van that came closest is driven by Mr. Ashok Varghese of the corner shop. 47.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed. 2 serious near-misses and 1 close pass were recorded. On 3 occasions the pedestrian was first to the conflict point.

One serious near-miss involved a car at 52.1 km/h with a PET of 0.4 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 9.8%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h. This is based on Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.

Another serious near-miss involved a car at 47.4 km/h with a PET of 1.1 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 6.7%.

A close pass involved a bus at 36.0 km/h with a PET of 2.4 s.

On engineering use of the counts, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 9.9 minutes. 47.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 1 gap of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 40.7 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and give pedestrians priority.

We would be pleased to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Garden Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We asked Crossing Watch to survey the Garden Road crossing. In 39.2 minutes of video 13 crossings and 30 vehicles were recorded, with an 85th percentile speed of 41.9 km/h.
There were 2 serious near-misses and 3 close passes. Serious means less than 1.5 s between pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot, close pass means 1.5 to 3.0 s. In 3 cases the person was first, in 2 the vehicle was first.
One serious near-miss involved a van at 34.5 km/h with a gap of 0.7 s, carrying an adult death risk of 2.2% if hit by a car front, which would be 0.6% at an impact speed of 20.0 km/h.
A second serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 30.8 km/h with a gap of 1.4 s, carrying an adult death risk of 1.6%.
A close pass involved a van at 38.1 km/h with a gap of 1.8 s, carrying an adult death risk of 1.4%.
A close pass involved a car at 32.6 km/h with a gap of 1.7 s, carrying an adult death risk of 1.1%.
A close pass involved an auto-rickshaw at 35.5 km/h with a gap of 1.8 s, carrying an adult death risk of 1.1%. Death-risk figures are from Rosen & Sander 2009 for adults aged 15 and over hit by a car front. A child struck at this spot would face about a 5% chance of being killed.
Engineering review notes PV2 was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8 from 20 pedestrians and 46 vehicles an hour scaled from 39.2 minutes of video, whereas a formal check counts the full peak hour. 43.0% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 5 such gaps and 2 of 12 s or more and the longest 68.6 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.
We request a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for people crossing. We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

Re: Safety outside Brook Street crossing

Crossing Watch video covering 20.2 minutes (1212.0 s) at Brook Street crossing recorded 15 crossings and 12 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 59.3 km/h.

Gaps where people crossed were limited: 12 gaps of 6 s or more were observed, with 0 gaps of 12 s or more, the longest gap was 6.2 s, and 78.6% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed.

In that period there were 3 serious near-misses (definition: pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s). Of these, 2 were person-first and 3 were vehicle-first, with 0 both at once.

Worst cases were:
A serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.0 s with a car travelling at 54.5 km/h. The modelled adult death risk if hit by the front of that car is 12.0% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.
A serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s with a car travelling at 37.0 km/h. The modelled adult death risk if hit by the front of that car is 2.7%.
A serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.9 s with a car travelling at 17.9 km/h. The modelled adult death risk if hit by the front of that car is 0.5%.
A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.8 s with a car travelling at 41.3 km/h. The modelled adult death risk if hit by the front of that car is 1.9%.
A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.2 s with a bus travelling at 32.9 km/h.

For context only, PV² was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8 based on 45 pedestrians and 36 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 20.2 minutes of video. This figure carries caveats: a formal check counts the full peak hour, pedestrians are people who walked 2 m or more on the marked carriageway, or anywhere in view if none is marked, and broken tracks can count one twice at 1.3x the true count in drone test, and the Union has told the Supreme Court that a Second Revision, IRC 103-2022, exists.
Similarly, the share of time in gaps (78.6% in gaps of 6 s or more) is from a short sample where the first and last gaps are cut short by the video; UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds while other groups, such as children, may need 10-12 s or longer.

We request that the authority provide a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and protect pedestrians.

We are happy to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority
Subject: Request for safety improvement at Park Avenue crossing

Dear Sir or Madam,

We write as the school using Park Avenue crossing to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table.

A 6.9 minute video (414.0 s) of the crossing recorded 4 pedestrian crossings and 22 moving vehicles.

In that time, 3 of 4 crossings (1 in 1.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 2 of 4 (1 in 2) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical: 19.4-99.4% and 6.8-93.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson); 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

We use the Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) definition where serious means pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass means 1.5-3.0 s.

The most serious near-miss involved a van at 54.1 km/h with 0.4 s between pedestrian and vehicle on the same spot. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 11.6%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

The second serious near-miss involved a car at 14.1 km/h with 0.8 s between pedestrian and vehicle on the same spot. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.4%, and it would remain 0.4% at an impact of 14.1 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.

A further close pass involved a car at 14.0 km/h with 2.5 s between pedestrian and vehicle on the same spot. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.0%, and it would be 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.

The 85th percentile speed in the recording was 59.4 km/h.

For context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 6.9 minutes. 70.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 8 gaps, 2 of them 12 s or more, longest 25.1 s (the first and last are cut short by the video).

We request the road authority install the raised zebra crossing with speed table and consider a 20 km/h zone with signs to reduce impact speeds and severance.

We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We write concerning the Station Road crossing and request a raised zebra crossing.

In 37.1 minutes (2226.0 s) of video at the Station Road crossing, 7 crossings and 6 vehicles were observed, with an 85th percentile speed of 57.2 km/h. During 37.1 minutes, 6 vehicles were seen.

4 of 7 crossings (1 in 1.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person.

3 of 7 crossings (1 in 2.3) were within 1.5 s.

One serious near-miss had a gap of 0.0 s with a car at 55.3 km/h.

The adult death risk if hit by a car front at 55.3 km/h is 12.7% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+).

Another serious near-miss had a gap of 1.0 s with a car at 49.2 km/h.

The adult death risk if hit at 49.2 km/h is 7.8%.

A third serious near-miss had a gap of 1.4 s with a car at 35.3 km/h.

The adult death risk if hit at 35.3 km/h is 2.4%.

A close pass had a gap of 1.7 s with a car at 39.8 km/h.

The adult death risk if hit at 39.8 km/h is 2.2%.

For reference, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 11 pedestrians and 10 vehicles an hour scaled from 37.1 minutes, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count 1.3x.

77.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 7 gaps, 2 of 12 s or more, and longest 31.3 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing to reduce speeds and give priority to people crossing.

We are happy to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at School Lane crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write on behalf of the school regarding the School Lane crossing. Crossing Watch measurements (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) over 43.7 minutes recorded 40 crossings and 28 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 65.6 km/h.

There were 4 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass defined as 1.5 to 3.0 s apart. In 3 cases the pedestrian arrived at the shared spot ahead of the moving vehicle.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 55 pedestrians and 38 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 43.7 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and pedestrians are people who walked 2 m or more on the marked carriageway with broken tracks able to count one twice.

In addition, 48.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 1 gap of 6 s or more and 0 gaps of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 6.4 s; the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

The most severe serious near-miss involved a car at 58.2 km/h with 0.2 s between pedestrian and vehicle on the same spot. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 15.9% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+), compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h limit.

A second serious near-miss involved a van at 55.6 km/h with 0.9 s between pedestrian and vehicle. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 13.1%, compared with 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h in a 20 km/h limit.

A third serious near-miss involved a van at 37.9 km/h with 0.0 s between pedestrian and vehicle. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 3.0%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h limit.

A fourth serious near-miss involved a bus at 37.8 km/h with 0.7 s between pedestrian and vehicle. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 2.9%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h limit.

A close pass involved a van at 58.3 km/h with 2.6 s between pedestrian and vehicle. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.3%, compared with 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h in a 20 km/h limit.

We request that you provide a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
Approved by The Principal

The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

Crossing Watch analysis (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) of 10.7 minutes (642.0 s) at Market Street crossing recorded 9 pedestrian crossings and 33 vehicles with an 85th percentile speed of 56.5 km/h.

In that period there were 5 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 1 close pass (1.5 s to 3.0 s).

Of the 5 serious cases, 4 involved the pedestrian arriving first, 1 involved the vehicle arriving first, and 1 involved both arriving at once.

76.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 8 gaps, 4 of them 12 s or more, longest 26.3 s.

Engineering note: PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 10.7, so those rates should be treated with caution.

Event 1 involved a bus at 57.8 km/h with a gap of 0.3 s.

For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 15.4% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), which would fall to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.

Event 2 involved an auto-rickshaw at 53.7 km/h with a gap of 0.0 s.

For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 11.3%, which would fall to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.

Event 3 involved a bus at 53.2 km/h with a gap of 0.5 s.

For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 10.8%, which would fall to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.

Event 4 involved a van at 27.9 km/h with a gap of 0.3 s.

For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 1.2%, which would fall to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.

Event 5 involved a car at 15.3 km/h with a gap of 0.2 s.

For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.4%, which would remain 0.4% at an impact of 15.3 km/h.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table to reduce speeds and increase safe gaps.

We are happy to share the video and data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We are writing about the crossing at Quarry Road crossing following a 10.1 minute video survey lasting 606.0 s.

During that time we counted 11 pedestrian crossings and 42 moving vehicles with an 85th percentile speed of 54.5 km/h. In total, 11 close passes were measured. A serious near miss is defined as a pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and a close pass is 1.5 to 3.0 s apart. We recorded 3 serious near misses and 3 close passes. For engineering context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 10.1 minutes, so they cannot be used here. 84.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 gaps of 6 s or more and 4 gaps of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 48.5 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video and that UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 13.5.2 states 4 to 6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds while other groups such as children may need 10 to 12 s or longer.

The worst events were as follows. One serious near miss involved a motorcycle at 52.9 km/h with 0.6 s between road users. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 10.5% based on Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+ and car fronts, compared with an impact speed of 17.7 km/h and death risk of 0.5% if the vehicle had been limited to 20 km/h.

A second serious near miss involved a bus at 37.6 km/h with 0.9 s between road users. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.9%, compared with an impact speed of 14.3 km/h and death risk of 0.4% at a 20 km/h limit.

A third serious near miss involved a car at 23.0 km/h with 0.3 s between road users. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.8%, compared with an impact speed of 20.0 km/h and death risk of 0.6% at a 20 km/h limit.

One close pass involved a car at 47.9 km/h with 1.5 s between road users. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 7.0%.

Another close pass involved a van at 43.4 km/h with 1.6 s between road users. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 3.8%.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce speeds and provide protected crossing priority.

We have the video and tracking data available and are happy to share them to support your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

Subject: Request for safer crossing at Lantern Road crossing

We write as the school beside Lantern Road crossing to request a safety improvement based on recent video measurements.

A 3.0 minute video (180.0 s) recorded 10 pedestrian crossings and 19 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 61.9 km/h. 8 gaps were cut short by the start or end of the video. Using the Crossing Watch definition, there were 3 serious near misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. There were 0 close passes in the 1.5-3.0 s range.

The worst near misses were as follows. One serious near miss involved a car at 57.0 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s. For that speed the estimated death risk for an adult hit by a car front is 14.6% from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
Another serious near miss involved a van at 56.8 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.0 s. For that speed the estimated death risk for an adult hit by a car front is 14.3%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
A third serious near miss involved a van at 13.4 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.9 s. For that speed the estimated death risk for an adult hit by a car front is 0.3%.

For context on exposure, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 3.0 minutes, so they are not reliable. Also, 72.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 8 gaps of 6 s or more and 8 gaps of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 55.6 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to provide priority and reduce vehicle speeds.

We are happy to share the video and tracking data for your review and to discuss next steps.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write on behalf of the school regarding the Lake View Road crossing.

We measured activity using Crossing Watch video (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) for 96.0 s (1.6 minutes). In that time we counted 10 pedestrian crossings and 7 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 43.5 km/h.

We recorded 3 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart.

The worst events were as follows. One serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.4 s with a car traveling at 21.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.7%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h, per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts. A second serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.5 s with a car traveling at 14.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.4%, compared with 0.4% at an impact of 14.2 km/h. A third serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.9 s with an auto-rickshaw traveling at 13.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.3%, compared with 0.3% at an impact of 13.2 km/h. One close pass had a time gap of 1.6 s with a car traveling at 40.7 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 3.0%, compared with 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h.

For context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 1.6. We also note 59.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 5 gaps, 4 of them 12 s or more, longest 12.0 s, with the first and last cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to slow traffic and provide priority for children and other pedestrians crossing. Most of the people seen crossing during the morning school run were unaccompanied children.

We are happy to share the video and underlying measurements to assist your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
Approved by The Principal on behalf of the school governing body

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at North Avenue crossing

Dear Sir or Madam,

We write on behalf of our school about the crossing on North Avenue outside our premises. Crossing Watch measurements from video with SAM tracking and road-plane geometry recorded 11 pedestrian crossings and 20 moving vehicles in 11.1 minutes (666.0 s). In 666.0 s there were 20 vehicles and 11 crossings.
The 85th percentile speed was 53.9 km/h.
There were 3 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart.
In that period 1 interaction had the person first, 2 had the vehicle first, and 1 had both at once.
One serious near-miss had a car at 55.5 km/h with a time gap of 1.1 s between pedestrian and vehicle.
Another serious near-miss had a car at 52.1 km/h with a time gap of 1.4 s between pedestrian and vehicle.
A third serious near-miss had a car at 29.4 km/h with a time gap of 0.0 s between pedestrian and vehicle.
A close pass had a car at 29.5 km/h with a time gap of 2.8 s between pedestrian and vehicle.
For adults hit by a car front the death-risk figures from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, are 13.0% at 55.5 km/h, 9.9% at 52.1 km/h, and 1.4% at 29.4 km/h.
At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed for the 29.4 km/h case would be 20.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.6%, and for the other cases the impact speed would be 0.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.0%.
PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 11.1 minutes, so those rates are not used for design.
70.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 10 gaps of 6 s or more and 1 gap of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 33.3 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.
We request installation of a raised zebra crossing at this location.
We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority
Subject: Request for safety improvement at Lake View Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning the crossing outside our school at Lake View Road crossing. A video survey of 3.9 minutes (234.0 s) recorded 10 pedestrian crossings and 4 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 23.9 km/h. 10 gaps were cut short by the start or end of the video.

Headline result: 1 of 10 crossings (1 in 10) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person; 1 of 10 (1 in 10) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical: 0.3-44.5% and 0.3-44.5% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson); 0.0-5.6 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There was 1 serious near-miss and 0 close passes. The definition used is serious: pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart; close pass: 1.5-3.0 s.

The most serious event was a serious near-miss involving a bus with a post-encroachment time of 1.2 s. The vehicle speed was 23.9 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.9% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 20.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.6%.

Engineering context is limited because PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 3.9 minutes. Counted: 10 pedestrian crossings, 4 moving vehicles. Also, 62.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 5 gaps, 4 of them 12 s or more, longest 50.2 s. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with 20 km/h zone signs at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for pedestrians.

We can share the full video and measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at the Market Street crossing

During 21.1 minutes of video at the Market Street crossing we recorded 31 crossings and 8 vehicles. 2 of 31 crossings (1 in 16) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 1 of 31 (1 in 31) had a vehicle within 1.5 s.

The most serious near-miss had a PET of 0.6 s. The vehicle involved was a van travelling at 22.6 km/h. A parent was injured here by a passing motorcycle earlier this year.
The adult death risk if hit at 22.6 km/h is 0.8% and at 20.0 km/h is 0.6% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

The second near-miss was a close pass with a PET of 2.0 s. The vehicle involved was a van travelling at 22.1 km/h.

The 85th percentile speed was 28.6 km/h. 95.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, based on 9 gaps with the longest 72.5 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, scaled from 21.1 minutes of video while a formal check counts the full peak hour.

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and protect people crossing.

We would be pleased to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write to request a safety improvement at the Orchard Lane crossing on behalf of the school.

A video survey of 26.2 minutes (1572.0 s) recorded 34 crossings and 33 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 53.2 km/h. Over 1572.0 s the count was 34 crossings and 33 vehicles with an 85th percentile speed of 53.2 km/h.

There were 4 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 close passes defined as 1.5 to 3.0 s apart.

In that period, 3 people crossed first before the vehicle and 3 vehicles passed first, with 0 cases of both at once.

One serious near-miss involved a bus at 55.8 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s, where Rosén & Sander 2009 data for adults 15+ hit by a car front gives a 13.3% adult death risk if hit, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h limit.

A second serious near-miss involved a car at 54.1 km/h with a gap of 0.8 s, with an 11.6% adult death risk if hit by a car front, compared to 0.0% at 0.0 km/h in a 20 km/h limit.

A third serious near-miss involved a car at 25.3 km/h with a gap of 0.4 s, with a 1.0% adult death risk if hit, compared to 0.6% at 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h limit.

A fourth serious near-miss involved a car at 16.0 km/h with a gap of 0.9 s, with a 0.4% adult death risk if hit, compared to 0.4% at 16.0 km/h in a 20 km/h limit.

One close pass involved a van at 47.7 km/h with a gap of 1.9 s, with a 2.6% adult death risk if hit, compared to 0.0% at 0.0 km/h in a 20 km/h limit.

We note for context that PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 78 pedestrians and 76 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 26.2 minutes of video, where a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice.

We also note that 43.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, based on 3 gaps of 6 s or more and 3 gaps of 12 s or more with a longest gap of 72.2 s, where the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements to assist your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

Subject: Request for safer crossing at Lantern Road crossing

We write as the school beside Lantern Road crossing to request a safety improvement based on recent video measurements.

A 3.0 minute video (180.0 s) recorded 10 pedestrian crossings and 19 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 61.9 km/h. Using the Crossing Watch definition, there were 3 serious near misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. There were 0 close passes in the 1.5-3.0 s range.

The worst near misses were as follows. One serious near miss involved a car at 57.0 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s. For that speed the estimated death risk for an adult hit by a car front is 14.6% from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
Another serious near miss involved a van at 56.8 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.0 s. For that speed the estimated death risk for an adult hit by a car front is 14.3%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.

Death risks are for adults 15+ hit by car fronts from Rosen and Sander 2009. At 20.0 km/h impact the modelled risk is 0.6%.

We request a raised zebra crossing at this spot to slow vehicles to near 20.0 km/h at the conflict point.

We will share the video and tracking on request to assist design.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Market Street crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school has reviewed video measurements of the Market Street crossing covering 32.3 minutes over 1938.0 s. In that period there were 32 crossings and 11 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 48.6 km/h. 1 crossing had the person go ahead of traffic, 1 had traffic go ahead of the person, and 2 had them go at the same time.

The analysis defined serious as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass as 1.5-3.0 s. There were 3 serious near-misses and 1 close pass.
One serious near-miss involved a bus at 50.7 km/h with a gap of 0.0 s. For an adult hit by a car front this speed carries an 8.8% death risk, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h, per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.
Another serious near-miss involved a van at 47.9 km/h with a gap of 0.0 s. For an adult hit by a car front this speed carries a 7.0% death risk, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
A third serious near-miss involved a car at 26.4 km/h with a gap of 0.1 s. For an adult hit by a car front this speed carries a 1.1% death risk, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
A close pass involved an auto-rickshaw at 40.2 km/h with a gap of 2.7 s.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 when scaled from 32.3 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice at 1.3x the true count in drone testing.
40.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 3 gaps of 6 s or more and 3 gaps of 12 s or more and longest gap 31.1 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you provide a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We would be happy to share the video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We are writing about the crossing outside our school at Cedar Lane crossing and ask you to make it safer.

A video of the crossing was measured using SAM tracking and road-plane geometry. In 11.2 minutes (672.0 s) there were eleven pedestrian crossings and 13 moving vehicles. 4 of 11 crossings (1 in 2.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 4 of 11 (1 in 2.8) within 1.5 s. If this recording is typical, the exact 95% ranges are 10.9-69.2% and 10.9-69.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). The 85th percentile speed was 50.4 km/h.

There were 4 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart.

A serious near-miss had a PET of 1.0 s involving an auto-rickshaw at 46.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 6.4% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 0.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.0%.

A serious near-miss had a PET of 0.1 s involving a van at 36.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.5%. At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 20.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.6%.

A serious near-miss had a PET of 0.8 s involving a van at 35.0 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.3%. At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 20.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.6%.

A serious near-miss had a PET of 0.7 s involving a motorcycle at 16.9 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.5%. At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 16.9 km/h with a death risk of 0.5%.

Engineering context with caveats: PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video, this one is 11.2 minutes with 11 pedestrian crossings and 13 moving vehicles. 47.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 12 gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 65.8 s, with the first and last gaps cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at Cedar Lane crossing to reduce vehicle speeds and give priority to people crossing.

We can share the video and the measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
Approved by The Principal as head of the school

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for raised zebra crossing at Lantern Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write as the school using Lantern Road crossing. A 36.0 minute video (2160.0 s) recorded 17 crossings and 30 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 55.3 km/h.

Of the 17 crossings, 6 of 17 (1 in 2.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 5 of 17 (1 in 3.4) within 1.5 s. The exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 14.2-61.7% and 10.3-56.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 2.2-13.1 and 1.6-11.7 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

There were 5 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 1 close pass (1.5-3.0 s). Most drivers were looking at their phones when they passed so close to pedestrians.

The most severe serious near-miss had a time gap of 1.0 s between the person and a bus travelling at 47.9 km/h, with an adult death risk of 7.0% if hit by a car front (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+).

A second serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.9 s with a car travelling at 47.7 km/h, with an adult death risk of 6.9% if hit.

A third serious near-miss had a time gap of 1.0 s with a car travelling at 28.5 km/h, with an adult death risk of 1.3% if hit.

A fourth serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.4 s with an auto-rickshaw travelling at 23.5 km/h, with an adult death risk of 0.8% if hit.

A fifth serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.3 s with a car travelling at 19.1 km/h, with an adult death risk of 0.6% if hit.

At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact speeds and adult death risks for these 5 events would be 0.0 km/h and 0.0%, 0.0 km/h and 0.0%, 20.0 km/h and 0.6%, 20.0 km/h and 0.6%, and 19.1 km/h and 0.6% respectively.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 (28 pedestrians and 50 moving vehicles an hour, scaled from 36 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count 1.3x the true count). 75.3% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 5 such gaps and 2 of them 12 s or more and longest 82.0 s, noting the first and last are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with 20 km/h approach signs at this location to reduce speeds and provide priority.

We are willing to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

I write on behalf of our school about safety at the Lantern Road crossing.

For an adult hit by a car front, the estimated death risk for the van event is 0.0%.

PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this video is 7.3 minutes with 5 pedestrian crossings and 5 moving vehicles.

81.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed.

I request installation of a raised zebra crossing to slow traffic and protect people crossing.

I offer to share the video for review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

We write about the Cedar Lane crossing. From video we measured 38.6 minutes (2316.0 s) at the site. In that time we counted 6 crossings and 13 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 58.0 km/h.

Using SAM tracking with road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time, we defined a serious near-miss as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and a close pass as 1.5 s to 3.0 s apart. We found 1 serious near-miss and 1 close pass. In the period 1 pedestrian was first and 1 vehicle was first.

The worst serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 19.1 km/h with a gap of 0.4 s to the pedestrian. For an adult hit by a car front at 19.1 km/h the death risk is 0.6% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.

The worst close pass involved a van at 58.6 km/h with a gap of 1.6 s to the pedestrian. For an adult hit by a car front at 58.6 km/h the death risk is 13.5% on the same basis.

For context, PV2 was 0.0 x 10^8 from 9 pedestrians and 20 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 38.6 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can double-count by 1.3x in our drone test. IRC:103-2012 cl. 6.7.4.1.2 notes a controlled crossing may be warranted above 1 x 10^8 on an undivided road and 2 x 10^8 on a divided road. Also 74.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 6 such gaps and 0 gaps of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 8.6 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We are willing to share the video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning the Lantern Road crossing outside our school.

A video survey of 26.7 minutes (1602.0 s) recorded 40 crossings and 7 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 62.7 km/h. Children hit at these speeds face a far higher risk of death than adults.

During that period there were 4 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass, defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart.

One serious near-miss involved a bus at 57.0 km/h with 0.7 s between road users.
Another serious near-miss involved a van at 45.5 km/h with 0.1 s between road users.
Another serious near-miss involved a car at 34.8 km/h with 1.3 s between road users.
A further serious near-miss involved a bus at 15.8 km/h with 0.8 s between road users.
The close pass involved a car at 44.4 km/h with 1.9 s between road users.

For adults hit by a car front, Rosén & Sander 2009 gives death risk of 14.5% at 57.0 km/h, 5.7% at 45.5 km/h, 2.3% at 34.8 km/h, 0.4% at 15.8 km/h and 1.9% at 44.4 km/h.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, based on 90 pedestrians and 16 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 26.7 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice at 1.3x the true count in drone tests.
63.2% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, from 12 gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 73.9 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing at Lake View Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school has commissioned a video review of the Lake View Road crossing. Over 26.1 minutes (1566.0 s) of video, Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) recorded 24 crossings and four vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 33.9 km/h. There was 1 serious near-miss and 0 close passes, where serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass is 1.5 to 3.0 s.

The worst case was a serious near-miss involving an auto-rickshaw with a PET of 1.4 s. The vehicle speed was 35.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed, the death-risk figure from Rosén & Sander 2009 is 2.4%.

For context, PV² was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8 from 55 pedestrians and 9 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 26.1 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and the video method can overcount pedestrians by 1.3x. Also, 89.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed from 11 gaps, 5 of them 12 s or more, longest 72.8 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location.

We are happy to share the video and data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at the North Avenue crossing

Respected Sir/Madam,

Our school monitors the North Avenue crossing outside our gate. In a 27.9 minute video (1674.0 s) Crossing Watch recorded 7 crossings and 40 moving vehicles.

The measurements show 6 of 7 crossings (1 in 1.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 2 of 7 (1 in 3.5) within 1.5 s. If this recording is typical, the exact 95% ranges are 42.1-99.6% and 3.7-71.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson), or 2.2-13.1 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There were 2 serious near-misses and 4 close passes. In 4 cases the person was first, in 2 the vehicle was first, and in 0 both were at once. The 85th percentile speed was 65.5 km/h. The recording showed 4 serious near-misses in all.

The worst event was a serious near-miss with PET of 0.6 s involving a motorcycle travelling at 50.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 8.6% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared to 0.6% at 19.7 km/h and an impact at 20 km/h limit conditions.
Another serious near-miss had PET of 1.2 s involving a motorcycle travelling at 39.5 km/h with an adult death risk if hit by a car front of 3.4%.
A close pass had PET of 1.6 s involving a car travelling at 58.1 km/h with an adult death risk if hit by a car front of 13.0%.
Another close pass had PET of 2.2 s involving a motorcycle travelling at 33.7 km/h.
A further close pass had PET of 2.2 s involving a bus travelling at 17.5 km/h.

For engineering context, PV² was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8 from 15 pedestrians and 86 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 27.9 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice (1.3x the true count in drone test).
Also 94.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 3 such gaps including 1 of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 33.6 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you provide a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce approach speeds and establish pedestrian priority.

We are willing to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements for your review and site inspection.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Canal Road crossing

We write from the school served by Canal Road crossing. A 30.2 minute video recording (1812.0 s) recorded 40 pedestrian crossings and 35 vehicles at the site.
5 of 40 crossings (1 in 8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 4 of 40 (1 in 10) were within 1.5 s, defined as serious.
The 85th percentile speed was 64.4 km/h. The closest of these passes was in fact a collision.
The worst serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 59.6 km/h with 0.1 s between person and vehicle on the same spot; if hit by a car front at that speed the risk of death for an adult is 17.8%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h, source Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.
A second serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 34.5 km/h with 1.1 s between person and vehicle; the adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 2.2%.
A third serious near-miss involved a bus at 18.7 km/h with 0.0 s between person and vehicle; the adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.5%.
A fourth serious near-miss involved a car at 14.1 km/h with 0.7 s between person and vehicle; the adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.4%.
A close pass involved an auto-rickshaw at 48.0 km/h with 2.1 s between person and vehicle; the adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 1.4%.
For engineering context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 79 pedestrians and 70 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 30.2 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and the pedestrian count method can overcount. 43.8% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, based on 1 gap with longest 8.2 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.
We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this crossing to reduce speeds and provide priority for people crossing.
We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at River Lane crossing

Respected Sir/Madam,

On behalf of the school adjoining River Lane crossing, I write to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table.

Crossing Watch video (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) observed River Lane crossing for 31.1 minutes (1866.0 s) and recorded 4 crossings and 25 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 55.4 km/h. In the near-miss with a time gap of 2.4 s, the auto-rickshaw reached the spot after the pedestrian.
There were 3 serious near-misses and 1 close pass. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart; close pass is 1.5-3.0 s. Of 4 interactions, 0 were person-first, 4 were vehicle-first, and 0 were both at once.
The near-miss between a pedestrian and a van at 46.6 km/h had a post-encroachment time of 0.9 s and an adult death risk if hit by a car front of 6.3%. At a 20 km/h limit the modelled impact speed is 0.0 km/h with adult death risk 0.0%.
The near-miss between a pedestrian and a car at 38.5 km/h had a post-encroachment time of 0.5 s and an adult death risk if hit by a car front of 3.1%. At a 20 km/h limit the modelled impact speed is 20.0 km/h with adult death risk 0.6%.
The near-miss between a pedestrian and a car at 28.4 km/h had a post-encroachment time of 0.2 s and an adult death risk if hit by a car front of 1.3%. At a 20 km/h limit the modelled impact speed is 20.0 km/h with adult death risk 0.6%.
The close pass between a pedestrian and an auto-rickshaw at 56.8 km/h had a post-encroachment time of 2.4 s and an adult death risk if hit by a car front of 1.0%. At a 20 km/h limit the modelled impact speed is 0.0 km/h with adult death risk 0.0%. Death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.
For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 8 pedestrians and 48 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 31.1 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and that pedestrian counts can be 1.3x the true count in our drone test.
Also, 77.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 12 gaps, 5 of them 12 s or more, longest 87.0 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.
We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table to reduce speeds and provide priority for pedestrians.
We offer to share the video and measurements for your review. Kindly consider the request on priority for school safety.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Road Authority,
In 29.4 minutes (1764.0 s) of video at Canal Road crossing, Crossing Watch using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time logged 21 crossings and 20 vehicles.
The 85th percentile speed was 52.1 km/h.
There were 4 serious near-misses with pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 2 close passes of 1.5-3.0 s.
5 had person stepping in before the vehicle, 1 had vehicle passing before the person, and 0 had both at once.
A serious near-miss had 0.6 s between road users and involved a car at 49.6 km/h, with 8.1% adult death risk if hit by a car front per Rosen and Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.
A serious near-miss had 1.2 s between road users and involved a motorcycle at 38.6 km/h, with 3.2% adult death risk if hit.
A serious near-miss had 0.1 s between road users and involved a car at 31.5 km/h, with 1.7% adult death risk if hit by a car front.
A serious near-miss had 1.2 s between road users and involved a motorcycle at 20.6 km/h, with 0.6% adult death risk if hit.
A close pass had 1.8 s between road users and involved a car at 37.1 km/h, with 1.3% adult death risk if hit by a car front.
PV2 was 0.0 x 10^8 from 43 pedestrians and 41 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 29.4 minutes of video, while a formal check counts the full peak hour.
85.4% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with video edges cutting gaps short.
There was 1 gap of 6 s or more, with 1 of 12 s or more, longest 57.8 s. In 29.4 minutes there were 21 crossings and 20 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 52.1 km/h and a longest vehicle-free gap of 57.8 s.
We request a raised zebra crossing at Canal Road crossing and offer to share the video for review.
Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write on behalf of the school beside the North Avenue crossing to request a safety improvement.

In 24.8 minutes (1488.0 s) of video at the crossing we recorded 12 crossings and 33 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 55.8 km/h.

6 of 12 crossings (1 in 2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 4 of 12 (1 in 3) were within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 21.1-78.9% and 9.9-65.1% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 2.2-13.1 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

Engineering context, briefly with caveats: PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 scaled from 24.8 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice at 1.3x the true count in our drone test. 89.8% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 8 gaps, 0 of them 12 s or more, longest 8.2 s, with the first and last cut short by the video. In those 24.8 minutes there were 8 gaps of 6 s or more and the longest gap was 8.2 s.

The worst near-misses were as follows. One serious near-miss had a gap of 0.1 s between person and a car travelling at 55.0 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 12.5% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), falling to 0.6% at 20.0 km/h. A second serious near-miss had a gap of 1.4 s with a car travelling at 49.8 km/h. A third serious near-miss had a gap of 1.4 s with a car travelling at 41.6 km/h. A fourth serious near-miss had a gap of 0.1 s with a motorcycle travelling at 28.2 km/h. A close pass had a gap of 2.0 s with a bus travelling at 21.1 km/h.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table to reduce speeds toward 20.0 km/h and provide protected priority for people crossing.

We are happy to share the video and SAM tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Lantern Road crossing

We write on behalf of the school regarding the crossing outside our premises at Lantern Road crossing.

In 19.1 minutes of video (1146.0 s) recorded at the crossing, Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) measured 9 crossings and 21 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 44.7 km/h. At its tightest, a vehicle and a person were on the same spot 1.3 s apart. In that period 6 of 9 crossings (1 in 1.5) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 4 of 9 (1 in 2.2) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 29.9-92.5% and 13.7-78.8% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 2.2-13.1 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There were 4 serious near-misses (less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s).

The worst events were:
A serious near-miss had 0.1 s between person and moving vehicle, a car at 40.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 3.7%, compared with 0.6% if impact were at 20.0 km/h (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
A serious near-miss had 1.1 s between person and moving vehicle, a bus at 39.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 3.3%, compared with 0.0% if impact were at 0.0 km/h.
A serious near-miss had 1.3 s between person and moving vehicle, a van at 31.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 1.7%, compared with 0.0% if impact were at 0.0 km/h.
A serious near-miss had 0.8 s between person and moving vehicle, a car at 26.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 1.1%, compared with 0.6% if impact were at 20.0 km/h.
A close pass had 2.8 s between person and moving vehicle, a van at 33.5 km/h.

For context from the engineering lines, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 28 pedestrians and 66 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 19.1 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice: 1.3x the true count in the drone test. Also 68.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 4 gaps, 2 of them 12 s or more, longest 26.5 s, noting the first and last are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements to assist your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We are writing about the crossing outside our school at Cedar Lane crossing and ask you to make it safer.

A video of the crossing was measured using SAM tracking and road-plane geometry. In 11.2 minutes (672.0 s) there were 11 pedestrian crossings and 13 moving vehicles. 4 of 11 crossings (1 in 2.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 4 of 11 (1 in 2.8) within 1.5 s. If this recording is typical, the exact 95% ranges are 10.9-69.2% and 10.9-69.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). The 85th percentile speed was 50.4 km/h.

There were 4 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart.

A serious near-miss had a PET of 1.0 s involving an auto-rickshaw at 46.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 6.4% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). A child struck at 46.8 km/h would have an estimated 15% risk of death. At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 0.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.0%.

A serious near-miss had a PET of 0.1 s involving a van at 36.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.5%. At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 20.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.6%.

A serious near-miss had a PET of 0.8 s involving a van at 35.0 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.3%. At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 20.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.6%.

A serious near-miss had a PET of 0.7 s involving a motorcycle at 16.9 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.5%. At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 16.9 km/h with a death risk of 0.5%.

Engineering context with caveats: PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video, this one is 11.2 minutes with 11 pedestrian crossings and 13 moving vehicles. 47.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 12 gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 65.8 s, with the first and last gaps cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at Cedar Lane crossing to reduce vehicle speeds and give priority to people crossing.

We can share the video and the measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
Approved by The Principal as head of the school

The review found 3 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s apart).

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Road Authority Officer, Crossing Watch video for 3.9 minutes at Station Road counted five pedestrian crossings and 28 moving vehicles with 85th speed of 54.1 km/h. 4 of 5 crossings (1 in 1.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person; 3 of 5 (1 in 1.7) within 1.5 s. We recorded 3 serious near-misses under 1.5 s and 1 close pass. The 0.0 s event involved a van at 47.6 km/h with adult death risk of 6.8% if hit by a car front, falling to 0.6% at 20 km/h with impact at 20.0 km/h. The 0.6 s event involved a bus at 52.1 km/h with adult death risk of 9.9% if hit by a car front, falling to 0.5% at 20 km/h with impact at 18.4 km/h. The 0.7 s event involved a bus at 26.1 km/h with adult death risk of 1.0% if hit by a car front, falling to 0.6% at 20 km/h with impact at 20.0 km/h. The 2.5 s close pass involved an auto-rickshaw at 22.0 km/h. PV2 needs at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 3.9 minutes. 73.5% of time was in gaps of 6 s or more, with 8 gaps and 3 gaps of 12 s or more up to 34.1 s. Please install a raised zebra crossing with 20 km/h approaches with signs. We will share the video on request. Yours faithfully, The Principal

To the road authority responsible for the Canal Road crossing:

During 4.8 minutes (288.0 s) of video, 12 pedestrian crossings and 27 moving vehicles were recorded, with 85th percentile speed of 50.8 km/h.

5 of 12 crossings (1 in 2.4) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 5 of 12 crossings (1 in 2.4) were within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical: 15.2-72.3% and 15.2-72.3% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson); 1.6-11.7 and 1.6-11.7 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

Of 12 crossings, 5 were serious near-misses with less than 1.5 s between pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot, with 0 close passes of 1.5-3.0 s. Counts were 3 with vehicle before person, 0 with person before vehicle, and 2 with simultaneous arrival. Most of the people crossing were young pupils hurrying to morning lessons.

The largest gap was 0.9 s between a person and an auto-rickshaw at 46.4 km/h, carrying 6.2% adult death risk if hit by a car front.

Another gap was 0.0 s between a person and a car at 41.9 km/h, carrying 4.2% adult death risk if hit by a car front.

Another gap was 0.3 s between a person and a car at 34.4 km/h, carrying 2.2% adult death risk if hit by a car front.

Another gap was 1.3 s between a person and a motorcycle at 28.0 km/h, carrying 1.2% adult death risk if hit by a car front.

Another gap was 0.0 s between a person and a car at 25.3 km/h, carrying 1.0% adult death risk if hit by a car front.

Death-risk figures are for adults 15+ hit by car fronts from Rosén & Sander 2009.

PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 4.8. 82.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, noting the video cuts the edge gaps short.

We request a raised zebra crossing at the Canal Road crossing.

We can share the video on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvements at Canal Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

I write as head of the school beside Canal Road crossing. A 38.2 minute video of the crossing recorded 38 crossings and 12 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 58.5 km/h.

In that period 2 of 38 crossings (1 in 19) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 2 of 38 (1 in 19) within 1.5 s. The 95% ranges if this recording is typical are 0.6-17.7% and 0.6-17.7% of crossings. There were 2 serious near-misses and 0 close passes.

The worst serious near-miss was 0.6 s apart with a car at 56.6 km/h, which carries a 14.1% adult death risk if hit by a car front, compared with 0.4% at an impact of 14.2 km/h at a 20 km/h limit.
The second serious near-miss was 0.9 s apart with a car at 56.1 km/h, which carries a 13.6% adult death risk for an adult hit by a car front.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, scaled from 38.2 minutes rather than a full peak hour and with counts that can be 1.3x high in our test. 90.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, based on 6 gaps with the first and last cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone and signage at this location. Both serious near-misses were caused by drivers exceeding the posted speed limit.

We are happy to share the video and measurements to assist your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the Garden Road crossing. Video measurements over 20.6 minutes, 1236.0 s, recorded 20 crossings and 19 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 54.1 km/h. This speed pattern shows that most drivers were exceeding the posted limit.

For crossing gaps, 66.3% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 1 gap of 6 s or more, 1 gap of 12 s or more, and longest gap 61.3 s. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

For exposure, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 58 pedestrians and 55 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 20.6 minutes of video. A formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice as 1.3x the true count in drone testing.

The serious near-miss had a gap of 1.0 s with a car at 56.6 km/h and an adult death risk of 14.1% if hit by a car front.
A close pass had a gap of 1.7 s with a car at 30.3 km/h and an adult death risk of 0.9% if hit.
A close pass had a gap of 1.5 s with a car at 17.7 km/h and an adult death risk of 0.5% if hit.
A close pass had a gap of 2.1 s with a car at 37.3 km/h and an adult death risk of 0.4% if hit.
A close pass had a gap of 1.7 s with a car at 19.6 km/h and an adult death risk of 0.3% if hit.
All death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.

We request a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for people crossing.

We can share the video and tracking data on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
