LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvements at the North Avenue crossing

I write on behalf of the school regarding the crossing outside our premises at the North Avenue crossing.

We arranged a video survey of the crossing. Measurements were made by Crossing Watch using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time. In 22.0 minutes (1320.0 s) of video, 5 crossings and 24 vehicles were recorded. The 85th percentile speed was 30.3 km/h. Mrs. Leela Fernandes, who drives the morning bus, caused the worst of these events.

In summary, 4 of 5 crossings (1 in 1.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 2 of 5 crossings (1 in 2.5) were within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 28.4-99.5% and 5.3-85.3% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson), and 1.1-10.2 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

Using the definitions of serious as less than 1.5 s apart and close pass as 1.5-3.0 s apart on the same spot, there were 2 serious near-misses and 2 close passes. Of the 4 conflicts, 1 had the person first and 3 had the vehicle first.

The worst near-misses were as follows. The most severe was a serious near-miss with a car at 25.3 km/h and 0.2 s between the person and the moving vehicle on the same spot. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 1.0% (0.6% at 20.0 km/h), per Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+.
A second serious near-miss involved a car at 12.5 km/h and 1.3 s apart. The adult death risk if hit is 0.3% (0.3% at 12.5 km/h).
A close pass involved a motorcycle at 30.7 km/h and 2.0 s apart. The adult death risk if hit is 0.3% (0.0% at 0.0 km/h).
A further close pass involved a car at 23.3 km/h and 2.7 s apart. The adult death risk if hit is 0.0% (0.0% at 0.0 km/h).

Engineering context: PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 14 pedestrians and 65 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 22 minutes of video. A formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice (1.3x the true count in our drone test). 75.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 2 gaps of 6 s or more, 2 of them 12 s or more, longest 86.2 s. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for pedestrians, particularly school children and families.

We are willing to share the video and the underlying measurements to assist your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Using the definitions of serious as less than 1.5 s apart and close pass as 1.5-3.0 s apart on the same spot, there were 2 serious near-misses and 2 close passes. Of the 4 conflicts, 1 had the person first and 3 had the vehicle first.

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning the Hill View Road crossing. A Crossing Watch video of 1.8 minutes (108.0 s) recorded 8 pedestrian crossings and 48 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 44.0 km/h. The van that came closest is driven by Mr. Ashok Varghese of the corner shop.

Engineering assessment is limited because PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 1.8. Within the recording, 43.8% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 9 gaps, 8 of them 12 s or more, longest 52.6 s (the first and last are cut short by the video).

In that same 1.8 minutes there were 4 serious near-misses and 2 close passes. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart; close pass is 1.5 s to 3.0 s.

One serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 36.8 km/h with 1.2 s between pedestrian and vehicle.

A second serious near-miss involved a car at 35.9 km/h with 0.2 s between users.

A third serious near-miss involved a car at 22.5 km/h with 0.1 s between users.

A fourth serious near-miss involved a car at 19.8 km/h with 1.0 s between users.

One close pass involved a car at 20.5 km/h with 2.0 s between users.

For adults hit by a car front, Rosén & Sander 2009 estimates adult death risk rises with impact speed. At these speeds adult risk was 2.7% at 36.8 km/h, 2.5% at 35.9 km/h, 0.8% at 22.5 km/h and 0.6% at 19.8 km/h. At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed and adult death risk would be lower, for example 20.0 km/h with 0.6% adult death risk.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing to slow vehicles and provide protected priority for pedestrians at this school crossing.

We are happy to share the video and SAM tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at River Lane crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school asked Crossing Watch to video River Lane crossing. In 42.6 minutes there were 18 crossings and 27 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 50.6 km/h. In the near-miss with a time gap of 2.3 s, the car reached the spot before the pedestrian.

Crossing Watch defines a serious near-miss as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and a close pass as 1.5 s to 3.0 s apart. There was 1 serious near-miss and 3 close passes. In 4 cases the pedestrian reached the conflict point first.

The serious near-miss had a gap of 0.1 s with a car at 14.9 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.4% from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+ car fronts, and at a 20 km/h limit the modelled impact speed would be 14.9 km/h with 0.4% adult death risk.

1 close pass had a gap of 1.5 s with a motorcycle at 53.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would be 11.1%, and at a 20 km/h limit the modelled impact speed would be 0.0 km/h with 0.0% adult death risk.

1 close pass had a gap of 2.3 s with a car at 44.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would be 0.3%, and at a 20 km/h limit the modelled impact speed would be 0.0 km/h with 0.0% adult death risk.

1 close pass had a gap of 2.0 s with a car at 18.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would be 0.0%, and at a 20 km/h limit the modelled impact speed would be 0.0 km/h with 0.0% adult death risk.

For engineering context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 scaled from 42.6 minutes to 25 pedestrians and 38 moving vehicles an hour, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour. In that video 50.9% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 gaps of 6 s or more and 9 of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 73.1 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone and signage at River Lane crossing to reduce speeds and protect children crossing.

We can share the full video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review. Please let us know what further data you need.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We are writing about the crossing at Quarry Road crossing following a 10.1 minute video survey lasting 606.0 s.

During that time we counted 11 pedestrian crossings and 42 moving vehicles with an 85th percentile speed of 54.5 km/h. Several children have been hurt at this crossing since the term began. A serious near miss is defined as a pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and a close pass is 1.5 to 3.0 s apart. We recorded 3 serious near misses and 3 close passes. For engineering context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 10.1 minutes, so they cannot be used here. 84.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 gaps of 6 s or more and 4 gaps of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 48.5 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video and that UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 13.5.2 states 4 to 6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds while other groups such as children may need 10 to 12 s or longer.

The worst events were as follows. One serious near miss involved a motorcycle at 52.9 km/h with 0.6 s between road users. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 10.5% based on Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+ and car fronts, compared with an impact speed of 17.7 km/h and death risk of 0.5% if the vehicle had been limited to 20 km/h.

A second serious near miss involved a bus at 37.6 km/h with 0.9 s between road users. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.9%, compared with an impact speed of 14.3 km/h and death risk of 0.4% at a 20 km/h limit.

A third serious near miss involved a car at 23.0 km/h with 0.3 s between road users. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.8%, compared with an impact speed of 20.0 km/h and death risk of 0.6% at a 20 km/h limit.

One close pass involved a car at 47.9 km/h with 1.5 s between road users. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 7.0%.

Another close pass involved a van at 43.4 km/h with 1.6 s between road users. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 3.8%.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce speeds and provide protected crossing priority.

We have the video and tracking data available and are happy to share them to support your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing outside school at Ring Road crossing

We measured the Ring Road crossing for 31.9 minutes and recorded 30 crossings and 34 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 62.1 km/h. The death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

In that period, 6 of 30 crossings (1 in 5) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 4 of 30 crossings (1 in 7.5) were within 1.5 s. The engineering note estimates PV² as 0.0 x 10^8 from 56 pedestrians and 64 vehicles per hour scaled from 31.9 minutes, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can overcount. 57.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with 4 such gaps, 2 of them 12 s or more, longest 75.0 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

The most serious near-misses were defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. One serious near-miss involved a bus at 56.4 km/h with 0.5 s between person and vehicle. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 13.9% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+ car fronts, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.
Another serious near-miss involved a car at 42.7 km/h with 0.5 s between person and vehicle. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 4.5% per Rosén & Sander 2009, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.
Another serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 21.3 km/h with 0.5 s between person and vehicle. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 0.7% per Rosén & Sander 2009, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.
Another serious near-miss involved a car at 14.3 km/h with 1.2 s between person and vehicle. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 0.4% per Rosén & Sander 2009, compared with 0.4% at 14.3 km/h.
A close pass involved an auto-rickshaw at 59.4 km/h with 2.3 s between person and vehicle. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 2.0% per Rosén & Sander 2009, compared with 0.0% at 0.0 km/h.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone signs at this location.

We have the video and Crossing Watch SAM tracking measurements and are willing to share them for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Brook Street crossing

We write concerning pedestrian safety at Brook Street crossing. Crossing Watch video analysis (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) of 22.9 minutes (1374.0 s) recorded 38 crossings and 10 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 55.0 km/h. There were 3 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart.

The most severe near-miss had a PET of 0.2 s involving a bus at 53.1 km/h. A second serious near-miss had a PET of 1.2 s involving a car at 49.1 km/h. A third serious near-miss had a PET of 0.3 s involving a car at 28.3 km/h. For context, Rosén & Sander 2009 estimates for adults 15+ hit by a car front give an adult death risk of 10.7% at 53.1 km/h, which would be 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit. The adult death risk was 7.7% at 49.1 km/h and 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit. The adult death risk was 1.3% at 28.3 km/h and 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit. In the 3 serious near-misses, the person was first in 1 case and the vehicle was first in 2 cases.

Engineering indicators were: PV² = 0.0 x 10^8 (100 pedestrians and 26 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 22.9 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice at 1.3x in drone tests) and 98.8% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with 10 gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 16.5 s (first and last gaps cut short by video).

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location and offer to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the Hill View Road crossing outside our school.

We had 10.9 minutes (654.0 s) of video analysed with SAM tracking and road-plane geometry. In that time there were 8 pedestrian crossings and 39 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 58.1 km/h. With this measure in place there will be no more fatalities here. 5 of 8 crossings (1 in 1.6) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person; 5 of 8 (1 in 1.6) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical: 24.5% to 91.5% and 24.5% to 91.5% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson); 1.6 to 11.7 and 1.6 to 11.7 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

Close passes are defined as 1.5 s to 3.0 s apart and serious near-misses as less than 1.5 s apart; there were 5 serious near-misses and 0 close passes. The worst cases were:

One serious near-miss had a car at 52.4 km/h with 0.9 s between pedestrian and vehicle, with an adult death risk of 10.1% if hit as a car front, falling to 0.0% at 20.0 km/h with impact at 0.0 km/h.
One serious near-miss had a bus at 44.6 km/h with 0.0 s between pedestrian and vehicle, with an adult death risk of 5.3% if hit, falling to 0.6% at 20.0 km/h with impact at 20.0 km/h.
One serious near-miss had a car at 32.4 km/h with 0.8 s between pedestrian and vehicle, with an adult death risk of 1.8% if hit, falling to 0.6% at 20.0 km/h with impact at 20.0 km/h.
One serious near-miss had a motorcycle at 24.8 km/h with 1.3 s between pedestrian and vehicle, with an adult death risk of 0.9% if hit, falling to 0.5% at 20.0 km/h with impact at 16.9 km/h.
One serious near-miss had a car at 22.0 km/h with 0.5 s between pedestrian and vehicle, with an adult death risk of 0.7% if hit, falling to 0.6% at 20.0 km/h with impact at 20.0 km/h.
All death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.

On gaps, 74.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 12 gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 56.3 s. PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 10.9 minutes, so PV² cannot be used here, and the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4 s to 6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds while other groups, such as children, may need 10 s to 12 s or longer.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this crossing to physically reduce approach speeds and give pedestrians priority.

We are happy to share the video and measurements and to meet on site.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning the crossing outside our school at Lake View Road crossing. A video survey of 3.9 minutes (234.0 s) recorded 10 pedestrian crossings and 4 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 23.9 km/h. Every person in these near-misses was a pupil of our school.

The most serious event was a serious near-miss involving a bus with a post-encroachment time of 1.2 s. The vehicle speed was 23.9 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.9% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 20.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.6%.

Engineering context is limited because PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 3.9 minutes. Counted: 10 pedestrian crossings, 4 moving vehicles. Also, 62.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 5 gaps, 4 of them 12 s or more, longest 50.2 s. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with 20 km/h zone signs at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for pedestrians.

We can share the full video and measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning the crossing outside our school at Lantern Road crossing. We arranged a Crossing Watch video analysis using SAM tracking and road-plane geometry. We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone and signs at this location. We would be pleased to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

A close pass (pet 2.5 s) involved an auto-rickshaw at 14.7 km/h.

A close pass (pet 2.8 s) involved a car at 45.0 km/h.

UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds while other groups, such as children, may need 10-12 s or longer.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h signs at this location.

We can share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing at River Lane crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school asked for a short video survey at River Lane crossing. The recording lasted 6.8 minutes (408.0 s). In that time 9 pedestrian crossings and 32 moving vehicles were counted. The 85th percentile speed was 30.4 km/h. 4 of 9 crossings (1 in 2.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 4 of 9 crossings (1 in 2.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 13.7-78.8% and 13.7-78.8% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

For engineering context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 6.8. Counted: 9 pedestrian crossings, 32 moving vehicles. 91.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 11 gaps, 10 of them 12 s or more, longest 86.0 s, with the first and last gaps cut short by the video. UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds and other groups, such as children, may need 10-12 s or longer.

The 4 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) included a car at 28.4 km/h with a gap of 1.2 s. For that car the estimated death risk if an adult is hit by a car front is 1.3%, compared with 0.4% at an impact of 14.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h.
A second serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 22.3 km/h with a gap of 0.2 s. For that motorcycle the provided adult death-risk figure is 0.7%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h.
A third serious near-miss involved a van at 12.1 km/h with a gap of 0.8 s. For that van the provided adult death-risk figure is 0.3%, compared with 0.3% at an impact of 12.1 km/h if limited to 20 km/h.
A fourth serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 12.0 km/h with a gap of 0.8 s. For that auto-rickshaw the provided adult death-risk figure is 0.3%, compared with 0.3% at an impact of 12.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h.
All death-risk figures are from Rosén & Sander 2009, for adults 15+ hit by car fronts. If a child had been hit in these events the chance of death would have been more than 10%.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at River Lane crossing.

We can share the video and the Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

At the Bridge Street crossing we recorded 6.2 minutes (372.0 s) of video. In that time we counted 5 pedestrian crossings and 15 moving vehicles, with 1 serious near-miss (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 close passes (1.5 s to 3.0 s apart).

A separate close pass had a gap of 1.9 s and involved a motorcycle at 35.8 km/h.

Another separate close pass had a gap of 2.2 s and involved a car at 24.2 km/h. Many drivers were traveling above the posted speed limit through this crossing area.

For context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this video is 6.2 minutes. 59.3 % of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, from 8 gaps with 4 of them 12 s or more and the longest 74.1 s, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide a safe, priority crossing for school children and other pedestrians.

We would be pleased to share the video and SAM tracking data on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide a safe, priority crossing for school children and other pedestrians.

We would be pleased to share the video and SAM tracking data on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write regarding the Canal Road crossing where we analysed 8.1 minutes (486.0 s) of video using SAM tracking and road-plane geometry.

In that time we counted 8 pedestrian crossings and 19 moving vehicles. During 8.1 minutes, 8 crossings, 19 vehicles, and 5 serious near-misses were logged.
The 85th percentile speed was 43.8 km/h.
We recorded 5 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 0 close passes, defined as 1.5-3.0 s.
The pedestrian was first in 2 cases and the vehicle first in 3 cases, with 0 cases both at once.
All death-risk figures below are for adults hit by a car front per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.

The most severe near-miss was a car at 40.0 km/h with 0.3 s between pedestrian and vehicle, carrying a 3.6% adult death risk if hit (0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h).
Another near-miss was a motorcycle at 36.9 km/h with 0.3 s gap, carrying a 2.7% adult death risk (0.6% at 20.0 km/h).
A third near-miss was a car at 23.6 km/h with 1.1 s gap, carrying a 0.8% adult death risk (0.6% at 20.0 km/h).
A fourth near-miss was a car at 19.3 km/h with 0.4 s gap, carrying a 0.6% adult death risk (0.6% at 19.3 km/h).
A fifth near-miss was a van at 17.5 km/h with 1.1 s gap, carrying a 0.5% adult death risk (0.5% at 17.5 km/h).

On engineering context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 8.1 minutes.
Separately, 72.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 10 gaps, 8 of them 12 s or more, longest 50.1 s, noting the first and last are cut short by the video.
UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds, while other groups, such as children, may need 10-12 s or longer.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce speeds and give pedestrians priority.
We are happy to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority regarding Canal Road crossing. Dear Sir/Madam, In 7.3 minutes (438.0 s) of video, Crossing Watch recorded 7 pedestrian crossings and 26 vehicles. 5 of 7 crossings (1 in 1.4) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s of the person, and 4 of 7 (1 in 1.8) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 29.0-96.3% and 18.4-90.1% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.6-11.7 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). Of the 5 near-misses, 4 were serious (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 1 was a close pass (1.5-3.0 s). 3 were person-first and 2 were vehicle-first. One serious near-miss had a PET of 0.2 s with a car at 57.3 km/h, with an adult death risk of 14.9% if hit (0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h). Another serious near-miss had a PET of 0.4 s with a motorcycle at 56.2 km/h, with an adult death risk of 13.7% if hit (0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h). Another serious near-miss had a PET of 0.1 s with a car at 52.6 km/h, with an adult death risk of 10.3% if hit (0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h). Another serious near-miss had a PET of 0.7 s with a bus at 21.6 km/h, with an adult death risk of 0.7% if hit (0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h). One close pass had a PET of 2.5 s with a car at 47.5 km/h. Death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, with no child risk stated. The 85th percentile speed was 64.3 km/h. Several schoolchildren had to sprint across during the busy morning drop-off to avoid being hit. Engineering context is limited: PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 7.3, with 7 pedestrian crossings and 26 moving vehicles counted. 52.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 9 gaps, 5 of them 12 s or more, longest 13.8 s, noting the first and last are cut short by the video. We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h markings at this location. We are willing to share the video and SAM tracking data for your review. Yours faithfully, The Principal Approved by The Principal on file review

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Canal Road crossing

From The Principal

We write to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table at the Canal Road crossing outside our school.

During a 31.3 minute video (1878.0 s) at this site, Crossing Watch recorded 24 crossings and 24 vehicles. 3 of 24 crossings (1 in 8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 2 of 24 (1 in 12) within 1.5 s. The 85th percentile speed was 34.5 km/h. Children hit at these speeds face a far higher risk of death than adults.

The 3 near-misses were as follows. One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.4 s with a bus at 21.9 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.7%, falling to 0.6% at 20 km/h (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.3 s with a bus at 20.7 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.6%. One close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.9 s with a motorcycle at 35.6 km/h.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 46 pedestrians and 46 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 31.3 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour. 96.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 6 such gaps including 1 of 12 s or more and longest 83.6 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request the raised zebra crossing described above and are happy to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority,

I write regarding the Station Road crossing used by our school. In 34.0 minutes of video we logged 10 crossings and 8 vehicles, with 85th percentile speed 32.3 km/h. By these figures the crossing already qualifies for a signal-controlled crossing. 3 of 10 crossings (1 in 3.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, while 2 of 10 (1 in 5) were within 1.5 s.

Of these events, 2 were serious and 1 was a close pass. The closest event was 0.3 s apart involving an auto-rickshaw at 32.0 km/h, with 1.8% adult death risk if hit by a car front, falling to 0.6% at 20.0 km/h impact. The next event was 0.2 s apart involving a motorcycle at 12.5 km/h, with 0.3% adult death risk if hit by a car front, unchanged at 0.3% at 12.5 km/h impact. The other event was 2.6 s apart involving a car at 16.4 km/h, with 0.0% adult death risk if hit by a car front.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 18 pedestrians and 14 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 34.0 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour. Also, 61.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with 10 gaps observed, noting edge video gaps are cut short by the video. Risk estimates use Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by car fronts.

We request a raised zebra crossing at this location. We offer to share the video for review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at North Avenue crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school monitors the North Avenue crossing. A Crossing Watch video (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) measured 31.7 minutes (1902.0 s) with 18 crossings and 43 vehicles. In that time 6 of 18 crossings (1 in 3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 3 of 18 (1 in 6) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 13.3-59.0% and 3.6-41.4% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 2.2-13.1 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson). The 85th percentile speed was 54.7 km/h. Most drivers were exceeding the posted 40 km/h speed limit through the crossing. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart; close pass is 1.5-3.0 s.

We recorded 3 serious near-misses and 3 close passes. One serious near-miss had a PET of 1.4 s with a car at 55.4 km/h. The adult death risk if hit at that speed is 12.8% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
A second serious near-miss had a PET of 1.3 s with a bus at 42.1 km/h. The adult death risk if hit at that speed is 4.3% on the same car-front basis.
A third serious near-miss had a PET of 0.3 s with a bus at 26.1 km/h. The adult death risk if hit at that speed is 1.0% on the same car-front basis.
One close pass had a PET of 1.5 s with a car at 47.0 km/h. The adult death risk if hit at that speed is 6.5%.
Another close pass had a PET of 1.5 s with an auto-rickshaw at 32.7 km/h. The adult death risk if hit at that speed is 1.9%.
All death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front and are not stated for children.

On engineering context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 34 pedestrians and 81 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 31.7 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour. Also 58.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 3 gaps and 1 of them 12 s or more and longest 23.7 s; the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to lower speeds and provide protected crossing gaps. We can share the full video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Park Avenue crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

I write on behalf of our school regarding the crossing outside our premises at Park Avenue crossing.

We commissioned a video survey of 35.3 minutes, which is 2118.0 s. In that time 3 crossings and 4 vehicles were observed. The 85th percentile speed was 23.9 km/h.

The survey recorded 1 serious near-miss, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. The worst case had a post-encroachment time of 0.7 s and involved an auto-rickshaw travelling at 22.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.8 percent. At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 20.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.6 percent for an adult, based on Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15 plus, car fronts.

For context, PV² was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8 from 5 pedestrians and 7 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 35.3 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour. Also, 74.1 percent of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Subject: Request for safer crossing at Canal Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We are writing about the Canal Road crossing outside our school. A video of 6.6 minutes (396.0 s) recorded 4 pedestrian crossings and 16 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 43.9 km/h. Had a child been struck, the impact would almost certainly have been fatal. 2 of 4 crossings (1 in 2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s, and 0 of 4 within 1.5 s.

There were 0 serious near-misses and 2 close passes, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot 1.5 to 3.0 s apart. One close pass involved a van at 12.7 km/h with a gap of 1.9 s.
The other close pass involved a motorcycle at 45.8 km/h with a gap of 2.6 s.

For context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this recording is 6.6 minutes with 4 crossings and 16 vehicles. 81.3% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, from 2 gaps with longest 8.4 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request a raised zebra crossing at this location to give pedestrians priority and reduce speeds.

We would be pleased to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at North Avenue crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school monitors the North Avenue crossing. A Crossing Watch video (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) measured 31.7 minutes (1902.0 s) with 18 crossings and 43 vehicles. In that time 6 of 18 crossings (1 in 3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 3 of 18 (1 in 6) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 13.3-59.0% and 3.6-41.4% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 2.2-13.1 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson). The 85th percentile speed was 54.7 km/h. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart; close pass is 1.5-3.0 s.

We recorded 3 serious near-misses and 3 close passes. One serious near-miss had a PET of 1.4 s with a car at 55.4 km/h. The adult death risk if hit at that speed is 12.8% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
A second serious near-miss had a PET of 1.3 s with a bus at 42.1 km/h. The adult death risk if hit at that speed is 4.3% on the same car-front basis.
A third serious near-miss had a PET of 0.3 s with a bus at 26.1 km/h. The adult death risk if hit at that speed is 1.0% on the same car-front basis.
One close pass had a PET of 1.5 s with a car at 47.0 km/h. The adult death risk if hit at that speed is 6.5%.
Another close pass had a PET of 1.5 s with an auto-rickshaw at 32.7 km/h. The adult death risk if hit at that speed is 1.9%.
All death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front and are not stated for children.

On engineering context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 34 pedestrians and 81 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 31.7 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour. Also 58.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 3 gaps and 1 of them 12 s or more and longest 23.7 s; the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. The longest gap with no moving vehicle where people crossed was 23.7 s.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to lower speeds and provide protected crossing gaps. We can share the full video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning the Cedar Lane crossing outside our school and enclose findings from a Crossing Watch survey using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time.

In 39.9 minutes (2394.0 s) of video, 39 crossings and 17 vehicles were observed, with an 85th percentile speed of 59.4 km/h. 4 gaps were cut short by the start or end of the video.

In that period 2 serious near-misses were recorded where pedestrian and moving vehicle were on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 1 close pass of 1.5-3.0 s was recorded, with 2 events person-first and 1 vehicle-first.

1 serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.5 s with a car travelling at 59.7 km/h.
That impact carries an adult death risk if hit of 17.9% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts, compared with 0.6% at an impact speed of 20.0 km/h.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.0 s with a car travelling at 23.0 km/h.
That impact carries an adult death risk if hit of 0.8%.
A close pass had a post-encroachment time of 2.2 s with a car travelling at 52.0 km/h.
That impact carries an adult death risk if hit of 1.4%.

For context, PV² was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8 for 59 pedestrians and 26 moving vehicles per hour scaled from 39.9 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count 1 person twice at 1.3x in our drone test.
Also 65.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, from 4 gaps with longest 11.5 s and 0 gaps of 12 s or more, noting first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide protected priority for pupils crossing.

We would be pleased to share the video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for raised zebra crossing at Lantern Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write as the school using Lantern Road crossing. A 36.0 minute video (2160.0 s) recorded 17 crossings and 30 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 55.3 km/h.

Of the 17 crossings, 6 of 17 (1 in 2.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 5 of 17 (1 in 3.4) within 1.5 s. The exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 14.2-61.7% and 10.3-56.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 2.2-13.1 and 1.6-11.7 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

There were 5 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 1 close pass (1.5-3.0 s).

The most severe serious near-miss had a time gap of 1.0 s between the person and a bus travelling at 47.9 km/h, with an adult death risk of 7.0% if hit by a car front (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+).

A second serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.9 s with a car travelling at 47.7 km/h, with an adult death risk of 6.9% if hit.

A third serious near-miss had a time gap of 1.0 s with a car travelling at 28.5 km/h, with an adult death risk of 1.3% if hit.

A fourth serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.4 s with an auto-rickshaw travelling at 23.5 km/h, with an adult death risk of 0.8% if hit.

A fifth serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.3 s with a car travelling at 19.1 km/h, with an adult death risk of 0.6% if hit.

At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact speeds and adult death risks for these 5 events would be 0.0 km/h and 0.0%, 0.0 km/h and 0.0%, 20.0 km/h and 0.6%, 20.0 km/h and 0.6%, and 19.1 km/h and 0.6% respectively.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 (28 pedestrians and 50 moving vehicles an hour, scaled from 36 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count 1.3x the true count). 75.3% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 5 such gaps and 2 of them 12 s or more and longest 82.0 s, noting the first and last are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with 20 km/h approach signs at this location to reduce speeds and provide priority.

We are willing to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at the Lantern Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school commissioned a video survey of the Lantern Road crossing. The recording lasted 2.1 minutes or 126.0 s and captured 7 pedestrian crossings and 25 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 52.3 km/h.

In that recording, 6 of 7 crossings (1 in 1.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 4 of 7 (1 in 1.8) were within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 42.1-99.6% and 18.4-90.1% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson), and 2.2-13.1 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

By definition a serious near-miss is pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and a close pass is 1.5-3.0 s apart. There were 4 serious near-misses and 2 close passes. In 3 instances the pedestrian arrived before the vehicle and in 3 instances the vehicle arrived before the pedestrian.

The worst events recorded were:
One serious near-miss with pet of 1.0 s involved a van at 42.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 4.3% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared with 0.0% at a 20 km/h limit with impact at 0.0 km/h.
One serious near-miss with pet of 0.2 s involved a van at 36.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.7%, compared with 0.6% at a 20 km/h limit with impact at 20.0 km/h.
One serious near-miss with pet of 0.4 s involved an auto-rickshaw at 33.7 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.1%, compared with 0.6% at a 20 km/h limit with impact at 20.0 km/h.
One serious near-miss with pet of 0.5 s involved a van at 18.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.5%, compared with 0.5% at a 20 km/h limit with impact at 18.5 km/h.
One close pass with pet of 1.8 s involved a motorcycle at 44.6 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.6%, compared with 0.0% at a 20 km/h limit with impact at 0.0 km/h.

Engineering data are limited: PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 2.1 minutes, with 7 pedestrian crossings and 25 moving vehicles counted. 74.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 2 such gaps and 1 of them 12 s or more, longest 49.9 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. For reference UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds while other groups, such as children, may need 10-12 s or longer.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for pedestrians.

We are willing to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) for your review and will cooperate with any site inspection.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the Cedar Lane crossing. In 22.2 minutes of video (1332.0 s) we recorded 34 crossings and 19 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 48.9 km/h.

4 of 34 crossings (1 in 8.5) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 4 of 34 (1 in 8.5) were within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical: 3.3-27.5% and 3.3-27.5% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson); 1.1-10.2 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There were 4 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 0 close passes (1.5-3.0 s). In 1 case the person was first and in 3 cases the vehicle was first.

The most serious near-misses were:
One serious near-miss involved a bus at 44.1 km/h with a gap of 0.7 s. For an adult hit by a car front at 44.1 km/h the death risk is 5.1%, compared with 0.5% at 20 km/h with impact at 18.8 km/h.
One serious near-miss involved a car at 36.6 km/h with a gap of 0.5 s. For an adult hit by a car front at 36.6 km/h the death risk is 2.7%, compared with 0.6% at 20 km/h with impact at 20.0 km/h.
One serious near-miss involved a car at 31.9 km/h with a gap of 1.3 s. For an adult hit by a car front at 31.9 km/h the death risk is 1.8%, compared with 0.0% at 20 km/h with impact at 0.0 km/h.
One serious near-miss involved a bus at 13.4 km/h with a gap of 1.0 s. For an adult hit by a car front at 13.4 km/h the death risk is 0.3%, compared with 0.3% at 20 km/h with impact at 13.4 km/h.
Risk figures are from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 92 pedestrians and 51 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 22.2 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour. 98.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 1 such gap, 0 of them 12 s or more, and longest 7.0 s; the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. Parents report that children regularly have to wait several minutes before they can cross safely.

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone with signs and markings at this crossing.

We can share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements and would welcome a site meeting.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

Subject: Request for safer crossing at Lantern Road crossing

We write as the school beside Lantern Road crossing to request a safety improvement based on recent video measurements.

A 3.0 minute video (180.0 s) recorded 10 pedestrian crossings and 19 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 61.9 km/h. These near-misses happened because drivers ignored the crossing markings. Using the Crossing Watch definition, there were 3 serious near misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. There were 0 close passes in the 1.5-3.0 s range.

The worst near misses were as follows. One serious near miss involved a car at 57.0 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s. For that speed the estimated death risk for an adult hit by a car front is 14.6% from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
Another serious near miss involved a van at 56.8 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.0 s. For that speed the estimated death risk for an adult hit by a car front is 14.3%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
A third serious near miss involved a van at 13.4 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.9 s. For that speed the estimated death risk for an adult hit by a car front is 0.3%.

For context on exposure, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 3.0 minutes, so they are not reliable. Also, 72.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 8 gaps of 6 s or more and 8 gaps of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 55.6 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to provide priority and reduce vehicle speeds.

We are happy to share the video and tracking data for your review and to discuss next steps.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning the Station Road crossing and request a raised zebra crossing.

In 37.1 minutes (2226.0 s) of video at the Station Road crossing, 7 crossings and 6 vehicles were observed, with an 85th percentile speed of 57.2 km/h. At its tightest, a vehicle and a person were on the same spot 1.7 s apart.

4 of 7 crossings (1 in 1.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person.

3 of 7 crossings (1 in 2.3) were within 1.5 s.

One serious near-miss had a gap of 0.0 s with a car at 55.3 km/h.

The adult death risk if hit by a car front at 55.3 km/h is 12.7% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+).

Another serious near-miss had a gap of 1.0 s with a car at 49.2 km/h.

The adult death risk if hit at 49.2 km/h is 7.8%.

A third serious near-miss had a gap of 1.4 s with a car at 35.3 km/h.

The adult death risk if hit at 35.3 km/h is 2.4%.

A close pass had a gap of 1.7 s with a car at 39.8 km/h.

The adult death risk if hit at 39.8 km/h is 2.2%.

For reference, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 11 pedestrians and 10 vehicles an hour scaled from 37.1 minutes, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count 1.3x.

77.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 7 gaps, 2 of 12 s or more, and longest 31.3 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing to reduce speeds and give priority to people crossing.

We are happy to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

Re: Safety request for Quarry Road crossing

We write to request a raised zebra crossing with speed table outside our school.

Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) measured the crossing for 9.0 minutes (540.0 s) and counted 5 pedestrian crossings and 6 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 58.1 km/h.

In that period there was 1 serious near-miss (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s). Person-first was 2 and vehicle-first was 1.

The most serious event had a PET of 0.4 s and involved a bus at 49.3 km/h. An adult hit by a car front at that speed would have a death risk of 7.8%, falling to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). A child struck at 49.3 km/h would have faced a 7.8% chance of dying.

A second event had a PET of 1.9 s and involved a van at 56.5 km/h. An adult hit by a car front at that speed would have a death risk of 5.6%.

A third event had a PET of 2.0 s and involved a motorcycle at 30.0 km/h. An adult hit by a car front at that speed would have a death risk of 0.3%.

PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 9.0. We also note that 52.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed. There were 8 gaps of 6 s and 1 gap of 12 s, longest 66.2 s, but the first and last are cut short by the video.

We ask the authority to install the raised zebra crossing with speed table noted above to reduce speeds and protect pedestrians. We are happy to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

A van at 17.9 km/h passed the same spot 0.7 s from the person, with 0.5% adult death risk if hit by a car front. A van at 15.3 km/h passed the same spot 1.7 s from the person, with 0.2% adult death risk if hit by a car front. Death risks from Rosen & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts. Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing at Lake View Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school has commissioned a video review of the Lake View Road crossing. Over 26.1 minutes (1566.0 s) of video, Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) recorded 24 crossings and 4 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 33.9 km/h. There was 1 serious near-miss and 0 close passes, where serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass is 1.5 to 3.0 s.

The worst case was a serious near-miss involving an auto-rickshaw with a PET of 1.4 s. The vehicle speed was 35.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed, the death-risk figure from Rosén & Sander 2009 is 2.4%.

For context, PV² was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8 from 55 pedestrians and 9 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 26.1 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and the video method can overcount pedestrians by 1.3x. Also, 89.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed from 11 gaps, 5 of them 12 s or more, longest 72.8 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. Over 26.1 minutes 24 crossings occurred with 4 vehicles, and 89.7% of the time fell in 11 gaps of 6 s or more, including 5 gaps of 12 s or more with the longest at 72.8 s.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location.

We are happy to share the video and data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority:

For Station Road crossing, video of 24.5 minutes / 1470.0 s showed 13 crossings and 24 vehicles with 85th percentile speed of 49.4 km/h.

4 of 13 crossings (1 in 3.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s, and 3 of 13 (1 in 4.3) within 1.5 s, with 95% Clopper-Pearson ranges of 9.1-61.4% and 5.0-53.8% and Poisson counts of 1.1-10.2 and 0.6-8.8.

Serious is less than 1.5 s apart and close pass is 1.5-3.0 s apart. We recorded 3 serious near-misses and 1 close pass, with 1 with person first and 2 with vehicle first and 1 with both at once.

An auto-rickshaw passed at 46.4 km/h with 0.6 s between road users, with 6.2% adult death risk if hit by a car front.
A car passed at 28.8 km/h with 1.0 s between road users, with 1.3% adult death risk if hit by a car front.
A van passed at 27.6 km/h with 0.0 s between road users, with 1.2% adult death risk if hit by a car front.
A car passed at 39.2 km/h with 2.3 s between road users.
At 20 km/h the modelled impact is 20.0 km/h with 0.6% adult death risk per Rosen and Sander for adults 15+ hit by car fronts.

PV2 was 0.0 x 10^8 from 32 pedestrians and 59 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 24.5 minutes, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour.
43.3% of time was in gaps of 6 s or more, from 4 gaps with 1 reaching 12 s or more and longest 32.1 s, noting gaps at start and end are cut short by the video.

Please provide a raised zebra crossing at Station Road crossing. We will share the video on request.

The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Bridge Street crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school asked Crossing Watch to review video of Bridge Street crossing. The video covered 8.9 minutes (534.0 s) and recorded 9 pedestrian crossings and 7 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 59.7 km/h. The van that came closest is driven by Mr. Ashok Varghese of the corner shop.

In that period there were 2 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart. The pedestrian was first in 2 cases and the vehicle was first in 1 case.

The worst events were: one serious near-miss with a gap of 0.5 s involving a car travelling at 55.5 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit by the car front would be 13.0% (0.6% at 20.0 km/h). A second serious near-miss had a gap of 0.1 s involving a car travelling at 31.0 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit would be 1.6% (0.6% at 20.0 km/h). A close pass had a gap of 1.5 s involving a car travelling at 31.4 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit would be 1.7% (0.0% at 20.0 km/h). Risk figures are from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by car fronts.

Engineering review notes that PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 8.9. It also notes that 55.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 3 such gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 48.4 s, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video and children may need 10-12 s or longer compared with the 4-6 s acceptable gap noted in UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) at urban speeds.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide a protected gap for pupils to cross. We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We are willing to share the video and data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We are writing about safety at the River Lane crossing outside our school. We made a video measurement of the crossing for 8.5 minutes (510.0 s). In that time we recorded 8 pedestrian crossings and 16 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 62.6 km/h.

In the recording, 2 of 8 crossings (1 in 4) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s of the person, and 1 of 8 crossings (1 in 8) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 3.2-65.1% and 0.3-52.7% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson), and 0.2-7.2 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

There was 1 serious near-miss (less than 1.5 s between pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot) and 1 close pass (1.5-3.0 s). 1 serious near-miss involved a van at 58.4 km/h with 0.6 s between person and vehicle on the same spot. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 16.2%, falling to 0.3% at 12.1 km/h if speed were limited to 20 km/h, per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts. 1 close pass involved a car at 27.2 km/h with 1.7 s between person and vehicle. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 0.7%, falling to 0.0% at 0.0 km/h if speed were limited to 20 km/h.

For context on engineering, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 8.5 minutes. 76.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone with signs at this location to reduce approach speeds and give pedestrians priority.

We would be happy to share the video and Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We are writing about pedestrian safety at the Mill Street crossing. 12 crossings and 17 vehicles were logged across 624.0 s of footage.

A 10.4 minute video (624.0 s) was analysed by Crossing Watch using SAM tracking and road-plane geometry. In that period 12 pedestrian crossings and 17 vehicles were counted, with an 85th percentile speed of 62.5 km/h. There were 7 gaps of 6 s or more, including 2 gaps of 12 s or more, and the longest gap was 43.1 s. In terms of engineering, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 10.4 minutes, and 41.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

During the observation there was 1 serious near-miss, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 5 close passes defined as 1.5 to 3.0 s apart. Of the interactions, 4 were person first, 2 were vehicle first and 0 were both at once.

The most serious event involved a bus at 13.9 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s.

For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.4%, from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+.

A separate close pass involved a motorcycle at 59.9 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 2.3 s.

For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.2%.

Another close pass involved a car at 33.6 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 2.2 s.

A further close pass involved a car at 41.4 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 2.6 s.

An additional close pass involved a van at 58.8 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 2.8 s.

To reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for people crossing, we request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements to support your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the Cedar Lane crossing. In 22.2 minutes of video (1332.0 s) we recorded 34 crossings and 19 vehicles. The 1332.0 s observation covered 34 crossings and 19 vehicles in 22.2 minutes. The 85th percentile speed was 48.9 km/h.

Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical: 3.3-27.5% and 3.3-27.5% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson); 1.1-10.2 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There were 4 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 0 close passes (1.5-3.0 s). In 1 case the person was first and in 3 cases the vehicle was first.

The most serious near-misses were:
One serious near-miss involved a bus at 44.1 km/h with a gap of 0.7 s. For an adult hit by a car front at 44.1 km/h the death risk is 5.1%, compared with 0.5% at 20 km/h with impact at 18.8 km/h.
One serious near-miss involved a car at 36.6 km/h with a gap of 0.5 s. For an adult hit by a car front at 36.6 km/h the death risk is 2.7%, compared with 0.6% at 20 km/h with impact at 20.0 km/h.
One serious near-miss involved a car at 31.9 km/h with a gap of 1.3 s. For an adult hit by a car front at 31.9 km/h the death risk is 1.8%, compared with 0.0% at 20 km/h with impact at 0.0 km/h.
One serious near-miss involved a bus at 13.4 km/h with a gap of 1.0 s. For an adult hit by a car front at 13.4 km/h the death risk is 0.3%, compared with 0.3% at 20 km/h with impact at 13.4 km/h.
Risk figures are from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 92 pedestrians and 51 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 22.2 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour. 98.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 1 such gap, 0 of them 12 s or more, and longest 7.0 s; the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone with signs and markings at this crossing.

We can share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements and would welcome a site meeting.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the Hill View Road crossing outside our school. A Crossing Watch review of 43.9 minutes of video recorded 18 crossings and 11 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 61.3 km/h. One near-miss ended with the vehicle hitting the person crossing.

The review defines serious as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass as 1.5 s to 3.0 s apart. In that period we recorded 1 serious near-miss and 3 close passes.

The serious near-miss had a gap of 1.4 s with an auto-rickshaw at 39.9 km/h.

One close pass had a gap of 2.2 s with a car at 57.8 km/h.

Another close pass had a gap of 1.8 s with an auto-rickshaw at 25.2 km/h.

The remaining close pass had a gap of 2.2 s with an auto-rickshaw at 34.8 km/h.

Based on Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by car fronts, the adult death risk if hit would be 3.5% at 39.9 km/h, 2.5% at 57.8 km/h, 0.4% at 25.2 km/h and 0.0% at 34.8 km/h, with 0.0% at the 20 km/h limit in each case.

The engineering notes recorded PV² as 0.0 x 10^8 when scaled from 43.9 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour.

They also recorded 56.2% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with 9 gaps, 4 of them 12 s or more and longest 16.3 s, with the caveat that first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request a raised zebra crossing on a speed table with 20 km/h markings at the crossing to reduce approach speeds.

We are willing to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Lantern Road crossing

We write on behalf of the school regarding the crossing outside our premises at Lantern Road crossing. During 19.1 minutes, 9 crossings and 21 vehicles were recorded.

In 19.1 minutes of video (1146.0 s) recorded at the crossing, Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) measured 9 crossings and 21 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 44.7 km/h. In that period 6 of 9 crossings (1 in 1.5) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 4 of 9 (1 in 2.2) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 29.9-92.5% and 13.7-78.8% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 2.2-13.1 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There were 4 serious near-misses (less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s).

The worst events were:
A serious near-miss had 0.1 s between person and moving vehicle, a car at 40.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 3.7%, compared with 0.6% if impact were at 20.0 km/h (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
A serious near-miss had 1.1 s between person and moving vehicle, a bus at 39.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 3.3%, compared with 0.0% if impact were at 0.0 km/h.
A serious near-miss had 1.3 s between person and moving vehicle, a van at 31.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 1.7%, compared with 0.0% if impact were at 0.0 km/h.
A serious near-miss had 0.8 s between person and moving vehicle, a car at 26.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 1.1%, compared with 0.6% if impact were at 20.0 km/h.
A close pass had 2.8 s between person and moving vehicle, a van at 33.5 km/h.

For context from the engineering lines, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 28 pedestrians and 66 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 19.1 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice: 1.3x the true count in the drone test. Also 68.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 4 gaps, 2 of them 12 s or more, longest 26.5 s, noting the first and last are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements to assist your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Cedar Lane crossing

We write concerning pedestrian safety at Cedar Lane crossing. The 6.1 minutes contained 12 crossings, 28 vehicles and 2 serious near-misses. Crossing Watch video analysis (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) measured 6.1 minutes (366.0 s) of activity, with 12 pedestrian crossings and 28 moving vehicles.

The 85th percentile vehicle speed was 43.0 km/h. Serious was defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and close pass as 1.5-3.0 s apart. In 6.1 minutes we recorded 2 serious near-misses and 2 close passes, with 2 events where the person was first and 2 where the vehicle was first.

The most severe event was a serious near-miss with a car at 38.8 km/h and a gap of 0.1 s. At that speed the published death-risk for an adult hit by a car front is 3.2%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A second serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 19.9 km/h with a gap of 1.4 s. At 19.9 km/h the same adult car-front risk reference is 0.6%.

A close pass involved a car at 32.3 km/h with a gap of 1.7 s. At that speed the adult car-front death risk is 1.1%, compared with 0.0% if impact had been at 0.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

A further close pass involved a car at 17.7 km/h with a gap of 2.9 s. At that speed the adult car-front death risk is 0.0%.

Engineering context must be read with caveats. PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this video is 6.1 minutes with 12 crossings and 28 vehicles, so it is too short for those rates. Separately, 90.8% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 7 gaps in total and 3 of them 12 s or more and the longest 60.1 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. For reference, UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds while other groups, such as children, may need 10-12 s or longer.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table at Cedar Lane crossing to reduce speeds and provide protected priority for the 12 crossings observed in 6.1 minutes.

We are happy to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

During 9.6 minutes (576.0 s) at the Canal Road crossing we recorded 11 pedestrian crossings and 22 vehicles with an 85th percentile speed of 43.7 km/h. This is what happens at the crossing on each day of the school week. 5 of 11 crossings (1 in 2.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s and 2 of 11 (1 in 5.5) within 1.5 s, with exact 95% ranges if this recording is typical of 16.7-76.6% and 2.3-51.8% (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.6-11.7 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). In total there were 2 serious near-misses and 3 close passes.

The most serious near-miss was 0.1 s between a pedestrian and a van at 26.5 km/h, with an adult death risk of 1.1% if hit by a car front (0.6% at 20.0 km/h). The second serious near-miss was 0.4 s between a pedestrian and a car at 22.3 km/h, with an adult death risk of 0.7% if hit by a car front (0.6% at 20.0 km/h). A close pass was 1.5 s with a bus at 12.8 km/h. A further close pass was 2.5 s with a van at 39.5 km/h. Another close pass was 2.8 s with a bus at 39.6 km/h. Risks are from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by car fronts.

PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 9.6 minutes. 99.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 6 such gaps including 6 gaps of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 49.1 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video and that the UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds while other groups such as children may need 10-12 s or longer.

We request a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and give pedestrians priority. We would be pleased to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning the Canal Road crossing outside our school. We commissioned a Crossing Watch analysis using SAM tracking and road-plane geometry with post-encroachment time, where serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass is 1.5-3.0 s.

In 9.9 minutes of video, which is 594.0 s, we counted 9 pedestrian crossings and 5 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 50.1 km/h. 9 gaps were cut short by the start or end of the video. 47.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed. 2 serious near-misses and 1 close pass were recorded. On 3 occasions the pedestrian was first to the conflict point.

One serious near-miss involved a car at 52.1 km/h with a PET of 0.4 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 9.8%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h. This is based on Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.

Another serious near-miss involved a car at 47.4 km/h with a PET of 1.1 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 6.7%.

A close pass involved a bus at 36.0 km/h with a PET of 2.4 s.

On engineering use of the counts, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 9.9 minutes. 47.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 1 gap of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 40.7 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and give pedestrians priority.

We would be pleased to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Bridge Street crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school asked Crossing Watch to review video of Bridge Street crossing. The video covered 8.9 minutes (534.0 s) and recorded 9 pedestrian crossings and 7 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 59.7 km/h.

In that period there were 2 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart. The pedestrian was first in 2 cases and the vehicle was first in 1 case.

The worst events were: one serious near-miss with a gap of 0.5 s involving a car travelling at 55.5 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit by the car front would be 13.0% (0.6% at 20.0 km/h). A second serious near-miss had a gap of 0.1 s involving a car travelling at 31.0 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit would be 1.6% (0.6% at 20.0 km/h). A close pass had a gap of 1.5 s involving a car travelling at 31.4 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit would be 1.7% (0.0% at 20.0 km/h). Risk figures are from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by car fronts.

Engineering review notes that PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 8.9. It also notes that 55.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 3 such gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 48.4 s, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video and children may need 10-12 s or longer compared with the 4-6 s acceptable gap noted in UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) at urban speeds.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide a protected gap for pupils to cross. We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We request a raised zebra crossing at this location.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for raised zebra crossing at Canal Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning safety at Canal Road crossing outside our school.

A video survey of 10.8 minutes (648.0 s) recorded 7 pedestrian crossings and 10 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 58.5 km/h.

In that time 2 of 7 crossings (1 in 3.5) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 2 of 7 (1 in 3.5) within 1.5 s.

There were 2 serious near-misses where pedestrian and moving vehicle were on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart.

The 1st serious near-miss had a gap of 1.3 s with a bus at 55.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 12.7% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared with 0.0% at a 20 km/h limit with impact at 0.0 km/h.

The 2nd serious near-miss had a gap of 0.1 s with a car at 54.2 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 11.7%, compared with 0.6% at a 20 km/h limit with impact at 20.0 km/h.

For context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 10.8 minutes.

50.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 10 gaps of 6 s or more, 8 of them 12 s or more and longest 15.5 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with 20 km/h zone signs to reduce vehicle speeds and protect children crossing.

We are willing to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Quarry Road crossing

A 9.8 minute video (588.0 s) at Quarry Road crossing recorded 3 pedestrian crossings and 4 moving vehicles with an 85th percentile speed of 35.7 km/h. In the near-miss with a time gap of 0.7 s, the auto-rickshaw reached the spot after the pedestrian.

The video showed 1 serious near-miss (defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 0 close passes (1.5-3.0 s).

The worst incident was a serious near-miss with a pet of 0.7 s involving an auto-rickshaw at 28.4 km/h. For adults 15+ hit by a car front (Rosén & Sander 2009), the death risk at that speed is 1.3% compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h limit.

PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 9.8. In the available video, 81.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 9 such gaps and longest 8.2 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request a raised zebra crossing with 20 km/h zone and signs at this location.

We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Road Authority Officer,

In 9.0 minutes of video at Cedar Lane crossing, 4 pedestrian crossings and 21 moving vehicles were recorded.
Measured speed reached 63.6 km/h for the 85th percentile. This is what happens at the crossing on each day of the school week.
3 of 4 crossings had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, with 2 of 4 within 1.5 s.
PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video, while this recording is 9.0 minutes with 4 pedestrian crossings and 21 moving vehicles.
40.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 2 gaps, 0 of 12 s or more, longest 8.5 s, with edge gaps cut short by the video.
The listed serious event had a pedestrian and a van on the same spot 0.1 s apart, with the van at 57.7 km/h, carrying 15.4% adult death risk if hit by a car front per Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by car fronts.
Another serious event had a pedestrian and a car on the same spot 0.4 s apart, with the car at 55.6 km/h, carrying 13.0% adult death risk if hit by a car front per Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by car fronts.
A separate close pass had a pedestrian and a car on the same spot 2.6 s apart, with the car at 59.0 km/h.
We request a raised zebra crossing at Cedar Lane crossing to slow vehicles and give pedestrians priority.
We can share the video and measurements for review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
