We write regarding the safety of the crossing outside our school on Bridge Street.

Crossing Watch measurements (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) for 33.9 minutes recorded 24 crossings and 23 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 51.2 km/h. The closest near-miss measured had a time gap of 1.2 s.

In that period 6 of 24 crossings (1 in 4) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 3 of 24 crossings (1 in 8) were within 1.5 s, classified as serious.

Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 9.8-46.7% for within 3 s and 2.7-32.4% for within 1.5 s (Clopper-Pearson), and 2.2-13.1 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The worst near-misses were as follows. One serious near-miss had a PET of 1.2 s with a car at 49.3 km/h and an adult death risk of 7.9% if hit. Another serious near-miss had a PET of 1.1 s with a motorcycle at 38.9 km/h and an adult death risk of 3.2% if hit. A third serious near-miss had a PET of 0.2 s with a car at 25.0 km/h and an adult death risk of 0.9% if hit. One close pass had a PET of 1.9 s with a car at 13.5 km/h. A further close pass had a PET of 2.8 s with a car at 33.3 km/h. Death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.

For context, PV² was estimated as 0.0 x 10^8 from 42 pedestrians and 41 vehicles an hour scaled from 33.9 minutes of video, with the caveat that broken tracks can count one person twice at 1.3x the true count in a drone test and a formal check counts the full peak hour. 46.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 gaps and 9 of them 12 s or more and longest 39.1 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location.

We would be pleased to share the Crossing Watch recording and measurements for your review and to discuss the site further.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Subject: Request to make the crossing outside the school safer - Bridge Street crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write regarding the safety of the crossing outside our school on Bridge Street.

Crossing Watch measurements (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) for 33.9 minutes recorded 24 crossings and 23 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 51.2 km/h. The video showed 9 gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle.

In that period 6 of 24 crossings (1 in 4) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 3 of 24 crossings (1 in 8) were within 1.5 s, classified as serious.

Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 9.8-46.7% for within 3 s and 2.7-32.4% for within 1.5 s (Clopper-Pearson), and 2.2-13.1 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The worst near-misses were as follows. One serious near-miss had a PET of 1.2 s with a car at 49.3 km/h and an adult death risk of 7.9% if hit. Another serious near-miss had a PET of 1.1 s with a motorcycle at 38.9 km/h and an adult death risk of 3.2% if hit. A third serious near-miss had a PET of 0.2 s with a car at 25.0 km/h and an adult death risk of 0.9% if hit. One close pass had a PET of 1.9 s with a car at 13.5 km/h. A further close pass had a PET of 2.8 s with a car at 33.3 km/h. Death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.

For context, PV² was estimated as 0.0 x 10^8 from 42 pedestrians and 41 vehicles an hour scaled from 33.9 minutes of video, with the caveat that broken tracks can count one person twice at 1.3x the true count in a drone test and a formal check counts the full peak hour. 46.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 gaps and 9 of them 12 s or more and longest 39.1 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location.

We would be pleased to share the Crossing Watch recording and measurements for your review and to discuss the site further.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We offer to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,

A third close pass had a PET of 1.8 s involving a bus at 21.9 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 0.3%.

We have the Crossing Watch video and tracking data using SAM road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time and are happy to share it.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the crossing on Garden Road outside our school.

In a 10.8 minute recording we counted 11 pedestrian crossings and 10 moving vehicles.
5 of 11 crossings (1 in 2.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person.
2 of 11 crossings (1 in 5.5) were within 1.5 s.
Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical: 16.7-76.6% and 2.3-51.8% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson); 1.6-11.7 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).
By definition, serious is less than 1.5 s apart and close pass is 1.5-3.0 s.

The worst incidents recorded were:
A car at 48.2 km/h was 0.6 s from a person, with adult death risk if hit of 7.1% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). The closest near-miss measured had a time gap of 0.6 s.
A van at 26.9 km/h was 0.7 s from a person, with adult death risk if hit of 1.1%.
A car at 51.0 km/h was 1.5 s from a person, with adult death risk if hit of 9.0%.
A car at 42.6 km/h was 1.6 s from a person, with adult death risk if hit of 3.6%.
A van at 23.8 km/h was 2.1 s from a person.
The 85th percentile speed was 56.8 km/h.
At a 20 km/h limit the adult death risk would be 0.6% for the 2 serious cases.

PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 10.8 minutes.
46.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed; 11 gaps, 9 of them 12 s or more, longest 20.2 s, with the first and last cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this crossing.
We offer to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the crossing on Market Street outside our school.

A video count of 4.4 minutes (264.0 s) recorded 7 pedestrian crossings and 8 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 58.5 km/h. 7 gaps were cut short by the start or end of the video. Of the 7 crossings, 2 of 7 (1 in 3.5) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 1 of 7 (1 in 7) within 1.5 s.

One serious near-miss left 0.8 s between pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot and involved a car at 53.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 11.0% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A second event was a close pass with 2.3 s between pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot and involved a bus at 12.3 km/h.

For context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video, so this 4.4 minute count with 7 crossings and 8 vehicles is too short to assess those rates. Also, 85.3% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, based on 4 gaps with longest 10.0 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with a raised table to slow vehicles and give priority to pupils crossing.

We can share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We write about the crossing on Cedar Lane outside our school. Crossing Watch video for 23.1 minutes (1386.0 s) recorded 16 crossings and 20 vehicles, with 85th percentile speed 59.9 km/h. The video showed 16 gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle.

Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical: 7.3-52.4% and 0.2-30.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson); 1.1-10.2 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The worst serious near-miss had PET 0.0 s involving a car at 50.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 8.7% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared with 0.6% at impact 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h limit.

Of the close passes, 1 had PET 1.7 s involving a car at 54.6 km/h. 1 had PET 1.5 s involving a bus at 30.4 km/h. 1 had PET 1.9 s involving a motorcycle at 23.2 km/h.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 42 pedestrians and 52 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 23.1 minutes, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can overcount by 1.3x. 90.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 3 such gaps and 2 of them 12 s or more and longest 87.5 s, with the caveat that first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone signs at this location.

We can share the video measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Lantern Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school monitors the crossing outside our gate on Lantern Road. In 44.2 minutes of video (2652.0 s) we recorded 15 crossings and 25 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 39.7 km/h. These near-misses happened because drivers ignored the crossing markings.

By definition a serious near-miss is pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and a close pass is 1.5 s to 3.0 s. We recorded 2 serious near-misses and 2 close passes. In 3 cases the pedestrian entered first and in 1 case the vehicle entered first, with 0 cases where both were at the conflict point at once.

1 serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.9 s with a bus at 28.7 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 1.3% (0.6% at a 20.0 km/h limit with impact at 20.0 km/h) per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.

1 serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.0 s with a car at 21.1 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 0.7% (0.6% at a 20.0 km/h limit with impact at 20.0 km/h).

1 close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.7 s with a car at 35.9 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 1.5% (0.0% at a 20.0 km/h limit with impact at 0.0 km/h).

1 close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.5 s with a car at 16.6 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 0.4% (0.4% at a 20.0 km/h limit with impact at 16.6 km/h).

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 20 pedestrians and 34 moving vehicles per hour scaled from 44.2 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can count 1 person twice (1.3x the true count in our drone test).

66.3% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 5 gaps and 5 of them 12 s or more and longest 13.8 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video and that UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4 s to 6 s as an acceptable gap at urban speeds while other groups such as children may need 10 s to 12 s or longer.

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone signs at this location to reduce speeds and provide priority.

We offer to share the full video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for a raised zebra crossing at the crossing studied on Park Avenue crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write as the school using the crossing outside our premises. A Crossing Watch analysis of 38.6 minutes of video recorded 32 crossings and 30 vehicles.
The 85th percentile speed was 63.7 km/h. 8 gaps were cut short by the start or end of the video.
In that period 5 of 32 crossings (1 in 6.4) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person.
Of those, 3 of 32 (1 in 11) were within 1.5 s.
The exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 5.3-32.8% and 2.0-25.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.6-11.7 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The worst near-misses recorded were as follows. A bus at 58.9 km/h was 1.0 s from a person on the same spot; the modelled adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 16.8% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
A motorcycle at 44.4 km/h was 0.5 s from a person on the same spot; the modelled adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 5.2%.
A car at 42.8 km/h was 1.2 s from a person on the same spot; the modelled adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 4.5%.
A car at 43.2 km/h was 2.3 s from a person on the same spot; the modelled adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.3%.
A car at 34.8 km/h was 2.6 s from a person on the same spot; the modelled adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.0%.
Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart; close pass is 1.5-3.0 s.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, calculated as 50 pedestrians and 47 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 38.6 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and our method can overcount pedestrians by 1.3x in drone tests.
Also 72.8% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, based on 8 gaps including 1 of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 60.4 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide protected priority for people crossing.
We are willing to share the underlying measurements and discuss the site in detail, and we can provide the video file on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write to request safety improvements at the crossing outside our school. Measurements from a video of the crossing were made by Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time).

In 5.5 minutes of recording (330.0 s) we recorded 5 pedestrian crossings and 9 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 57.3 km/h. 6 gaps were cut short by the start or end of the video. In this recording 2 of 5 crossings (1 in 2.5) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, including 1 of 5 (1 in 5) within 1.5 s.

The most serious near-miss was an auto-rickshaw at 59.4 km/h with a gap of 1.1 s to the person on the same spot, carrying an adult death risk of 17.4% if hit by a car front (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). A second close pass was a car at 57.5 km/h with a gap of 1.9 s to the person on the same spot, carrying an adult death risk of 6.1% if hit by a car front.

On engineering review, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this recording is 5.5 minutes with 5 crossings and 9 vehicles, so they cannot be assessed. For gaps, 87.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 6 such gaps including 5 of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 16.7 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce speeds and provide a protected crossing point.

We would be pleased to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

Crossing Watch analysis (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) of 10.7 minutes (642.0 s) at Market Street crossing recorded 9 pedestrian crossings and 33 vehicles with an 85th percentile speed of 56.5 km/h. In one of these events the vehicle struck the pedestrian.

In that period there were 5 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 1 close pass (1.5 s to 3.0 s).

Of the 5 serious cases, 4 involved the pedestrian arriving first, 1 involved the vehicle arriving first, and 1 involved both arriving at once.

76.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 8 gaps, 4 of them 12 s or more, longest 26.3 s.

Engineering note: PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 10.7, so those rates should be treated with caution.

Event 1 involved a bus at 57.8 km/h with a gap of 0.3 s.

For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 15.4% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), which would fall to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.

Event 2 involved an auto-rickshaw at 53.7 km/h with a gap of 0.0 s.

For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 11.3%, which would fall to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.

Event 3 involved a bus at 53.2 km/h with a gap of 0.5 s.

For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 10.8%, which would fall to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.

Event 4 involved a van at 27.9 km/h with a gap of 0.3 s.

For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 1.2%, which would fall to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.

Event 5 involved a car at 15.3 km/h with a gap of 0.2 s.

For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.4%, which would remain 0.4% at an impact of 15.3 km/h.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table to reduce speeds and increase safe gaps.

We are happy to share the video and data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing outside our school

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about pedestrian safety outside our school. A video review using SAM tracking and road-plane geometry measured the crossing for 37.5 minutes (2250.0 s). In that time 22 crossings and 20 vehicles were counted.

Of the 22 crossings, 3 of 22 (1 in 7.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 
Of the 22 crossings, 2 of 22 (1 in 11) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 1.5 s of the person. 
Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 2.9-34.9% and 1.1-29.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). The 85th percentile vehicle speed was 61.3 km/h. In total, 2 close passes were measured.

The worst near-miss was a serious case with a car at 31.7 km/h passing 0.2 s from a person. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 1.7% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
Another serious case was a bus at 24.2 km/h with a gap of 1.0 s. For an adult hit at that speed the death risk is 0.9%, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
A close pass was a van at 57.7 km/h with a gap of 2.4 s.

For context, PV² was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8 from 35 pedestrians and 32 moving vehicles an hour scaled from the 37.5 minutes of video, noting that a formal check counts the full peak hour. 
In addition, 84.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, from 12 gaps with longest 9.2 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this crossing.

We are happy to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

During 9.6 minutes (576.0 s) at the Canal Road crossing we recorded 11 pedestrian crossings and 22 vehicles with an 85th percentile speed of 43.7 km/h. 5 of 11 crossings (1 in 2.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s and 2 of 11 (1 in 5.5) within 1.5 s, with exact 95% ranges if this recording is typical of 16.7-76.6% and 2.3-51.8% (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.6-11.7 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). In total there were 2 serious near-misses and 3 close passes.

The most serious near-miss was 0.1 s between a pedestrian and a van at 26.5 km/h, with an adult death risk of 1.1% if hit by a car front (0.6% at 20.0 km/h). This shows a child struck at 26.5 km/h in this crossing would almost certainly have been killed. The second serious near-miss was 0.4 s between a pedestrian and a car at 22.3 km/h, with an adult death risk of 0.7% if hit by a car front (0.6% at 20.0 km/h). A close pass was 1.5 s with a bus at 12.8 km/h. A further close pass was 2.5 s with a van at 39.5 km/h. Another close pass was 2.8 s with a bus at 39.6 km/h. Risks are from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by car fronts.

PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 9.6 minutes. 99.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 6 such gaps including 6 gaps of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 49.1 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video and that the UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds while other groups such as children may need 10-12 s or longer.

We request a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and give pedestrians priority. We would be pleased to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about safety at the Orchard Lane crossing. Crossing Watch monitoring (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) for 18.0 minutes recorded 5 pedestrian crossings and 5 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 46.5 km/h. In total, 4 close passes were measured.

We identified 2 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s). In 3 cases the person reached the conflict point first and in 1 case the vehicle did.

1 serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 43.2 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.5 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 4.7% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+), compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.

1 serious near-miss involved a van at 34.1 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.1%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.

1 close pass involved a motorcycle at 22.7 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 2.4 s.

1 close pass involved a car at 34.4 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 2.6 s.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 (17 pedestrians and 17 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 18.0 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can overcount by 1.3x). 89.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed (4 gaps of 6 s or more, 4 of 12 s or more, longest 80.0 s; the first and last gaps are cut short by the video).

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to lower speeds and provide pedestrian priority.

We can share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing at River Lane crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school asked for a short video survey at River Lane crossing. The recording lasted 6.8 minutes (408.0 s). In 6.8 minutes there were 32 moving vehicles and 9 crossings, with 4 serious cases where the gap was less than 1.5 s and the longest gap without a vehicle was 86.0 s. In that time 9 pedestrian crossings and 32 moving vehicles were counted. The 85th percentile speed was 30.4 km/h. 4 of 9 crossings (1 in 2.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 4 of 9 crossings (1 in 2.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 13.7-78.8% and 13.7-78.8% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

For engineering context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 6.8. Counted: 9 pedestrian crossings, 32 moving vehicles. 91.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 11 gaps, 10 of them 12 s or more, longest 86.0 s, with the first and last gaps cut short by the video. UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds and other groups, such as children, may need 10-12 s or longer.

The 4 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) included a car at 28.4 km/h with a gap of 1.2 s. For that car the estimated death risk if an adult is hit by a car front is 1.3%, compared with 0.4% at an impact of 14.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h.
A second serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 22.3 km/h with a gap of 0.2 s. For that motorcycle the provided adult death-risk figure is 0.7%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h.
A third serious near-miss involved a van at 12.1 km/h with a gap of 0.8 s. For that van the provided adult death-risk figure is 0.3%, compared with 0.3% at an impact of 12.1 km/h if limited to 20 km/h.
A fourth serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 12.0 km/h with a gap of 0.8 s. For that auto-rickshaw the provided adult death-risk figure is 0.3%, compared with 0.3% at an impact of 12.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h.
All death-risk figures are from Rosén & Sander 2009, for adults 15+ hit by car fronts.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at River Lane crossing.

We can share the video and the Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We write concerning safety outside our school at Bridge Street crossing.

We are happy to share the recording data and video for your review and to discuss next steps.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We are writing about pedestrian safety at the Mill Street crossing.

A 10.4 minute video (624.0 s) was analysed by Crossing Watch using SAM tracking and road-plane geometry. In that period 12 pedestrian crossings and 17 vehicles were counted, with an 85th percentile speed of 62.5 km/h. There were 7 gaps of 6 s or more, including 2 gaps of 12 s or more, and the longest gap was 43.1 s. In terms of engineering, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 10.4 minutes, and 41.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

Of the interactions, 4 were person first, 2 were vehicle first and 0 were both at once. Many of the speeding drivers were parents rushing to drop off their children.

The most serious event involved a bus at 13.9 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s.

For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.4%, from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+.

A separate close pass involved a motorcycle at 59.9 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 2.3 s.

For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.2%.

Another close pass involved a car at 33.6 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 2.2 s.

A further close pass involved a car at 41.4 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 2.6 s.

An additional close pass involved a van at 58.8 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 2.8 s.

To reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for people crossing, we request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements to support your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing outside school on Hill View Road

We measured traffic at the crossing on Hill View Road for 39.3 minutes. In that time we observed 34 crossings and 21 vehicles. The 85th-percentile speed was 60.0 km/h. The recording showed 2 serious near-misses in all.

We recorded 4 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 close passes of 1.5 s to 3.0 s. In 1 case the person was there first and in 5 cases the vehicle was there first.

The most severe near-miss involved a car at 56.6 km/h with a gap of 0.7 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 14.1% based on Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults aged 15 and above.
Another serious near-miss involved a car at 28.6 km/h with a gap of 0.3 s. The estimated adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 1.3%.
A further serious near-miss involved a bus at 26.0 km/h with a gap of 0.1 s.
A fourth serious near-miss involved a car at 25.1 km/h with a gap of 0.6 s. The estimated adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 1.0%.

Engineering indicators were calculated as follows. PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 52 pedestrians and 32 vehicles per hour scaled from the video, noting that a formal check requires the full peak hour and that broken tracks can overcount pedestrians by 1.3x in drone tests. 45.3% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for children crossing. We are willing to share the video and measurement file for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing outside school on Hill View Road

We measured traffic at the crossing on Hill View Road for 39.3 minutes. In that time we observed 34 crossings and 21 vehicles. The 85th-percentile speed was 60.0 km/h. The video showed 12 gaps of 12 s or more with no moving vehicle.

We recorded 4 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 close passes of 1.5 s to 3.0 s. In 1 case the person was there first and in 5 cases the vehicle was there first.

The most severe near-miss involved a car at 56.6 km/h with a gap of 0.7 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 14.1% based on Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults aged 15 and above.
Another serious near-miss involved a car at 28.6 km/h with a gap of 0.3 s. The estimated adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 1.3%.
A further serious near-miss involved a bus at 26.0 km/h with a gap of 0.1 s.
A fourth serious near-miss involved a car at 25.1 km/h with a gap of 0.6 s. The estimated adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 1.0%.

Engineering indicators were calculated as follows. PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 52 pedestrians and 32 vehicles per hour scaled from the video, noting that a formal check requires the full peak hour and that broken tracks can overcount pedestrians by 1.3x in drone tests. 45.3% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for children crossing. We are willing to share the video and measurement file for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Park Avenue crossing

We write concerning the Park Avenue crossing outside our school.

A video survey of 36.5 minutes recorded 18 crossings and 43 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 59.5 km/h. There were 6 of 18 crossings (1 in 3) with a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s, and 4 of 18 (1 in 4.5) within 1.5 s.

Definition used was serious: pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart; close pass: 1.5 to 3.0 s. Overall the footage held 4 serious near-misses and 2 close passes.

The worst serious near-miss involved a van at 57.5 km/h with 0.2 s between road users. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 15.1% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts, compared to 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.

A second serious near-miss involved a bus at 35.8 km/h with 0.0 s between road users. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.5%, compared to 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.

A third serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 29.7 km/h with 1.3 s between road users. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 1.4%, compared to 0.0% at 0.0 km/h.

A fourth serious near-miss involved a car at 15.9 km/h with 0.9 s between road users. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.4%, compared to 0.4% at 15.9 km/h.

A close pass involved a car at 30.6 km/h with 1.7 s between road users. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 1.0%, compared to 0.0% at 0.0 km/h.

Engineering context from the same recording: PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 30 pedestrians and 71 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 36.5 minutes of video, where broken tracks can count one twice at 1.3x the true count in drone testing. 60.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 5 gaps and 4 of them 12 s or more and longest 40.4 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this crossing.

We can share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Canal Road crossing

We write from the school served by Canal Road crossing. A 30.2 minute video recording (1812.0 s) recorded 40 pedestrian crossings and 35 vehicles at the site.
5 of 40 crossings (1 in 8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 4 of 40 (1 in 10) were within 1.5 s, defined as serious.
The 85th percentile speed was 64.4 km/h.
The worst serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 59.6 km/h with 0.1 s between person and vehicle on the same spot; if hit by a car front at that speed the risk of death for an adult is 17.8%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h, source Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.
A second serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 34.5 km/h with 1.1 s between person and vehicle; the adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 2.2%.
A third serious near-miss involved a bus at 18.7 km/h with 0.0 s between person and vehicle; the adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.5%.
A fourth serious near-miss involved a car at 14.1 km/h with 0.7 s between person and vehicle; the adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.4%.
A close pass involved an auto-rickshaw at 48.0 km/h with 2.1 s between person and vehicle; the adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 1.4%.
For engineering context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 79 pedestrians and 70 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 30.2 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and the pedestrian count method can overcount. 43.8% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, based on 1 gap with longest 8.2 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.
We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this crossing to reduce speeds and provide priority for people crossing.
We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Lantern Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school monitors the crossing outside our gate on Lantern Road. In 44.2 minutes of video (2652.0 s) we recorded 15 crossings and 25 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 39.7 km/h.

By definition a serious near-miss is pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and a close pass is 1.5 s to 3.0 s. We recorded 2 serious near-misses and 2 close passes. In 3 cases the pedestrian entered first and in 1 case the vehicle entered first, with 0 cases where both were at the conflict point at once.

1 serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.9 s with a bus at 28.7 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 1.3% (0.6% at a 20.0 km/h limit with impact at 20.0 km/h) per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.

1 serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 1.0 s with a car at 21.1 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 0.7% (0.6% at a 20.0 km/h limit with impact at 20.0 km/h).

1 close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.7 s with a car at 35.9 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 1.5% (0.0% at a 20.0 km/h limit with impact at 0.0 km/h).

1 close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.5 s with a car at 16.6 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 0.4% (0.4% at a 20.0 km/h limit with impact at 16.6 km/h).

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 20 pedestrians and 34 moving vehicles per hour scaled from 44.2 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can count 1 person twice (1.3x the true count in our drone test).

66.3% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 5 gaps and 5 of them 12 s or more and longest 13.8 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video and that UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4 s to 6 s as an acceptable gap at urban speeds while other groups such as children may need 10 s to 12 s or longer.

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone signs at this location to reduce speeds and provide priority.

We offer to share the full video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Lake View Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We recorded activity at Lake View Road crossing for 17.9 minutes (1074.0 s). That 17.9 minute recording contained 30 crossings and 14 vehicles. In that time we counted 30 crossings and 14 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 45.5 km/h.

Of 30 crossings, 4 of 30 (1 in 7.5) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s of the person and 2 of 30 (1 in 15) within 1.5 s. If this recording is typical, the exact 95% ranges are 3.8-30.7% and 0.8-22.1% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There was 1 serious near-miss where the person was first, 3 where the vehicle was first, and 0 where both were at once.

One serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 44.9 km/h with 1.4 s between the person and vehicle. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would be 5.4% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

Another serious near-miss involved a bus at 26.8 km/h with 1.0 s between the person and vehicle. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would be 1.1%.

One close pass involved a car at 21.3 km/h with 2.0 s between the person and vehicle. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would be 0.0%.

Another close pass involved a bus at 23.4 km/h with 2.3 s between the person and vehicle. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would be 0.0%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, from 101 pedestrians and 47 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 17.9 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count 1.3x.

52.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 1 such gap and a longest gap of 11.4 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for people crossing.

We are happy to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
The Principal will add approval name and date on signing.

Dear Road Authority,

We are writing about the Garden Road crossing used by our school. In 11.2 minutes of video we counted 7 pedestrian crossings and 8 moving vehicles with 85th percentile speed 27.3 km/h.

1 of 7 crossings (1 in 7) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 1 of 7 crossings (1 in 7) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical: 0.4-57.9% and 0.4-57.9% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson). 0.0-5.6 and 0.0-5.6 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The worst serious near-miss left 0.6 s between the person and a van. The van was travelling at 24.2 km/h. For adults 15+ hit by car fronts the death risk at that speed is 0.9% (Rosén & Sander 2009). At 20.0 km/h the adult death risk would be 0.6%.

PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video. This one is 11.2. 96.3% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed.

We request a raised zebra crossing at this location. We are happy to share the video for review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

During 9.6 minutes (576.0 s) at the Canal Road crossing we recorded 11 pedestrian crossings and 22 vehicles with an 85th percentile speed of 43.7 km/h. 5 of 11 crossings (1 in 2.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s and 2 of 11 (1 in 5.5) within 1.5 s, with exact 95% ranges if this recording is typical of 16.7-76.6% and 2.3-51.8% (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.6-11.7 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). In total there were 2 serious near-misses and 3 close passes.

The most serious near-miss was 0.1 s between a pedestrian and a van at 26.5 km/h, with an adult death risk of 1.1% if hit by a car front (0.6% at 20.0 km/h). The second serious near-miss was 0.4 s between a pedestrian and a car at 22.3 km/h, with an adult death risk of 0.7% if hit by a car front (0.6% at 20.0 km/h). A close pass was 1.5 s with a bus at 12.8 km/h. A further close pass was 2.5 s with a van at 39.5 km/h. Another close pass was 2.8 s with a bus at 39.6 km/h. Risks are from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by car fronts.

PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 9.6 minutes. 99.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 6 such gaps including 6 gaps of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 49.1 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video and that the UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds while other groups such as children may need 10-12 s or longer.

We request a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and give pedestrians priority. We would be pleased to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

Subject: Request for safer crossing at Lantern Road crossing

We write as the school beside Lantern Road crossing to request a safety improvement based on recent video measurements.

A 3.0 minute video (180.0 s) recorded 10 pedestrian crossings and 19 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 61.9 km/h. Using the Crossing Watch definition, there were 3 serious near misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. There were 0 close passes in the 1.5-3.0 s range.

The worst near misses were as follows. One serious near miss involved a car at 57.0 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s. For that speed the estimated death risk for an adult hit by a car front is 14.6% from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
Another serious near miss involved a van at 56.8 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.0 s. For that speed the estimated death risk for an adult hit by a car front is 14.3%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
A third serious near miss involved a van at 13.4 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.9 s. For that speed the estimated death risk for an adult hit by a car front is 0.3%.

For context on exposure, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 3.0 minutes, so they are not reliable. Also, 72.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 8 gaps of 6 s or more and 8 gaps of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 55.6 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to provide priority and reduce vehicle speeds.

We are happy to share the video and tracking data for your review and to discuss next steps.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Road Authority,

At Orchard Lane crossing, Crossing Watch video for 18.7 minutes, 1122.0 s duration, recorded 35 crossings and 19 vehicles with 85th percentile speed of 52.0 km/h.

Serious means pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and close pass means 1.5-3.0 s apart. There were 2 serious near-misses and 1 close pass, with 1 person first and 2 vehicle first and 0 both at once.

The serious near-miss with a van at 45.2 km/h was 0.8 s apart, with 5.6% adult death risk if hit by a car front, falling to 0.2% at 9.4 km/h impact under a 20 km/h limit.
The serious near-miss with a car at 39.2 km/h was 0.7 s apart, with 3.3% adult death risk if hit by a car front, falling to 0.6% at 20.0 km/h impact under a 20 km/h limit.

Death risks are for adults 15+ hit by car fronts.

PV2 was 0.0 x 10^8 from 112 pedestrians and 61 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 18.7 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour.
98.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with 12 gaps, 7 of them 12 s or more, longest 55.0 s, noting edge gaps are cut short by the video.

We request a raised zebra crossing at Orchard Lane crossing. We offer to share the video for review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We write about safety at the Orchard Lane crossing.

In 4.9 minutes (294.0 s) of video, Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) recorded 12 pedestrian crossings and 7 moving vehicles.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table to slow traffic toward 20.0 km/h.

We can share the full video and measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

The estimated adult death risk if hit by the car front was 1.2%, per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts. At a 20 km/h limit the modelled impact was 19.6 km/h with death risk of 0.6%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 73 pedestrians and 9 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 32.9 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour. 93.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, from 11 gaps with 8 of them 12 s or more and longest 84.2 s, noting the 1st and last are cut short by the video.

We offer to share the video and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing at River Lane crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

Our school asked for a short video survey at River Lane crossing. The recording lasted 6.8 minutes (408.0 s). In that time 9 pedestrian crossings and 32 moving vehicles were counted. The 85th percentile speed was 30.4 km/h. 11 gaps were cut short by the start or end of the video. 4 of 9 crossings (1 in 2.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 4 of 9 crossings (1 in 2.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 13.7-78.8% and 13.7-78.8% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

For engineering context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 6.8. Counted: 9 pedestrian crossings, 32 moving vehicles. 91.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 11 gaps, 10 of them 12 s or more, longest 86.0 s, with the first and last gaps cut short by the video. UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds and other groups, such as children, may need 10-12 s or longer.

The 4 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) included a car at 28.4 km/h with a gap of 1.2 s. For that car the estimated death risk if an adult is hit by a car front is 1.3%, compared with 0.4% at an impact of 14.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h.
A second serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 22.3 km/h with a gap of 0.2 s. For that motorcycle the provided adult death-risk figure is 0.7%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h.
A third serious near-miss involved a van at 12.1 km/h with a gap of 0.8 s. For that van the provided adult death-risk figure is 0.3%, compared with 0.3% at an impact of 12.1 km/h if limited to 20 km/h.
A fourth serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 12.0 km/h with a gap of 0.8 s. For that auto-rickshaw the provided adult death-risk figure is 0.3%, compared with 0.3% at an impact of 12.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h.
All death-risk figures are from Rosén & Sander 2009, for adults 15+ hit by car fronts.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at River Lane crossing.

We can share the video and the Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Road Authority,

I am writing as head of the school by Market Street crossing to request a safety improvement based on a 2.8 minute video recording (168.0 s).

What was measured: 4 pedestrian crossings and 5 moving vehicles were counted. Most crossings involved young children walking alone. The 85th percentile speed was 50.5 km/h. 2 of 4 crossings (1 in 2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 2 of 4 (1 in 2) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 6.8-93.2% and 6.8-93.2% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.2-7.2 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There were 2 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 0 close passes (1.5-3.0 s).

The worst near-misses were as follows. One serious near-miss had a PET of 1.4 s with a car at 52.6 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 10.3% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 0.0 km/h with an adult death risk of 0.0%.
Another serious near-miss had a PET of 0.3 s with a car at 15.7 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.4% (same source). At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact would be 15.7 km/h with an adult death risk of 0.4%.

Context on gaps: 44.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 12 gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 36.7 s. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video. PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 2.8 minutes with 4 pedestrian crossings and 5 moving vehicles, so rates are indicative only.

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone with signs at Market Street crossing to reduce speeds and provide protected crossing time.

We are willing to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Lantern Road crossing

We write on behalf of the school regarding the crossing outside our premises at Lantern Road crossing.

In 19.1 minutes of video (1146.0 s) recorded at the crossing, Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) measured 9 crossings and 21 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 44.7 km/h. In that period 6 of 9 crossings (1 in 1.5) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 4 of 9 (1 in 2.2) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 29.9-92.5% and 13.7-78.8% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 2.2-13.1 and 1.1-10.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There were 4 serious near-misses (less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s).

The worst events were:
A serious near-miss had 0.1 s between person and moving vehicle, a car at 40.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 3.7%, compared with 0.6% if impact were at 20.0 km/h (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
A serious near-miss had 1.1 s between person and moving vehicle, a bus at 39.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 3.3%, compared with 0.0% if impact were at 0.0 km/h.
A serious near-miss had 1.3 s between person and moving vehicle, a van at 31.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 1.7%, compared with 0.0% if impact were at 0.0 km/h.
A serious near-miss had 0.8 s between person and moving vehicle, a car at 26.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the estimated death risk is 1.1%, compared with 0.6% if impact were at 20.0 km/h.
A close pass had 2.8 s between person and moving vehicle, a van at 33.5 km/h.

For context from the engineering lines, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 28 pedestrians and 66 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 19.1 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice: 1.3x the true count in the drone test. We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location. Children using this crossing face a 3.7% chance of death on every school trip.

We would be pleased to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements to assist your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning the School Lane crossing. From video of 2.0 minutes (120.0 s) we measured 10 pedestrian crossings and 3 moving vehicles.

The 85th-percentile speed was 62.8 km/h. 3 of 10 crossings (1 in 3.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 2 of 10 (1 in 5) were within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical: 6.7-65.2% and 2.5-55.6% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson); 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

Worst measured near-misses were: a serious near-miss with PET of 0.5 s involving a bus at 54.9 km/h (adult death risk if hit by car front 12.3% per Rosén & Sander 2009; at a 20 km/h limit impact 20.0 km/h with risk 0.6%). A separate serious near-miss had PET of 1.3 s involving a motorcycle at 40.2 km/h (adult death risk 3.6%; at 20 km/h limit impact 0.0 km/h with risk 0.0%). A separate close pass had PET of 1.7 s involving an auto-rickshaw at 48.2 km/h (adult death risk 4.6%; at 20 km/h limit impact 0.0 km/h with risk 0.0%).

For context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 2.0. Counted: 10 pedestrian crossings, 3 moving vehicles. Also 96.3% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 3 gaps, 2 of them 12 s or more, longest 55.7 s, with the first and last cut short by the video. UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds; other groups, such as children, may need 10-12 s or longer.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone signs at this location. This volume alone proves the site already meets the national warrant for a signalised crossing.

We can share the video and measurement log on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning the Market Street crossing outside our school. Crossing Watch recorded 11.6 minutes of video covering six pedestrian crossings and 13 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 29.7 km/h.

Headline results were 3 of 6 crossings (1 in 2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s of the person and 2 of 6 (1 in 3) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 11.8-88.2% and 4.3-77.7% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart; close pass is 1.5-3.0 s.

The worst near-misses were as follows. One serious near-miss had a PET of 0.3 s with a car at 30.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 1.5% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), which would be 0.6% at impact of 20.0 km/h with a 20 km/h limit.

A second serious near-miss had a PET of 1.3 s with a car at 14.7 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.4%, which would remain 0.4% at impact of 14.7 km/h with a 20 km/h limit.

A close pass had a PET of 2.2 s with a car at 26.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front the death risk data shows 0.0% at that speed, and 0.0% at impact of 0.0 km/h with a 20 km/h limit.

Engineering context is limited: PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 11.6 minutes with 6 pedestrian crossings and 13 moving vehicles. 52.8% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 5 gaps and 0 of them 12 s or more and longest 9.8 s, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds and other groups, such as children, may need 10-12 s or longer.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone with signs at this location.

We can share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety works at Bridge Street crossing

We write from the school beside Bridge Street crossing. Crossing Watch measured the crossing for 25.8 minutes and recorded 32 crossings and 15 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 47.4 km/h.

There was 1 serious near-miss, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass, defined as 1.5 to 3.0 s apart. The serious near-miss involved a bus at 46.0 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s. The close pass involved a bus at 22.2 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 1.7 s.

For adults hit by a car front, Rosén & Sander 2009 estimates the death risk at 46.0 km/h as 5.9% and at 22.2 km/h as 0.4%. At a 20.0 km/h limit the estimated impact speed for the worst case would be 20.0 km/h with 0.6% adult death risk, and for the second case 2.5 km/h with 0.1% adult death risk.

Engineering notes from the video: PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, scaled from 25.8 minutes of video, while a formal check counts the full peak hour. 55.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 4 gaps of 6 s or more, 2 of them 12 s or more and longest 86.2 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request a raised zebra crossing on a speed table with 20 km/h zone signs and markings at this location. We will share the full video and data on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority
Subject: Request for safety improvements at Bridge Street crossing

We are writing to request a raised zebra crossing at Bridge Street crossing following video measurements at the site.

During 41.5 minutes of video we recorded 18 crossings and 3 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 43.8 km/h.
There were 0 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 close passes (1.5 s to 3.0 s apart).
1 close pass involved a car at 26.4 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 1.7 s; for an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.7 % (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
1 other close pass involved a motorcycle at 44.3 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 2.3 s.
For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 scaled from 41.5 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and with caveats about counting.
71.8 % of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.
We request installation of a raised zebra crossing to reduce speeds and provide a protected crossing point.
We can share the Crossing Watch video (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry) on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Brook Street crossing

We write concerning the Brook Street crossing outside our school. A 6.2 minute video recording (372.0 s) counted 9 pedestrian crossings and 29 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 62.5 km/h.

In that recording, 4 of 9 crossings (1 in 2.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 2 of 9 (1 in 4.5) were within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 13.7-78.8% and 2.8-60.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

The most severe events were 2 serious near-misses and 2 close passes. One serious near-miss involved a car at 49.2 km/h with a gap of 0.9 s. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 7.8% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). At 20 km/h the death risk would be 0.0%.
Another serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 14.0 km/h with a gap of 1.0 s. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.4%. At 20 km/h the death risk would be 0.4%.
A close pass involved an auto-rickshaw at 59.2 km/h with a gap of 2.4 s. The adult death risk if hit at that speed is 1.3%.
A further close pass involved a car at 25.7 km/h with a gap of 1.8 s. The adult death risk if hit at that speed is 0.4%.

For context on gaps, 41.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 12 gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 58.1 s (the first and last are cut short by the video). PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 6.2. Counted: 9 pedestrian crossings, 29 moving vehicles.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for pupils crossing. I can't create a misleading sentence to insert into a letter to a road authority because it would introduce claims not supported by the measurements and could mislead safety decisions.

We are willing to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning the Lantern Road crossing outside our school.

A video survey of 26.7 minutes (1602.0 s) recorded 40 crossings and 7 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 62.7 km/h.

During that period there were 4 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass, defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart.

One serious near-miss involved a bus at 57.0 km/h with 0.7 s between road users.
Another serious near-miss involved a van at 45.5 km/h with 0.1 s between road users.
Another serious near-miss involved a car at 34.8 km/h with 1.3 s between road users.
A further serious near-miss involved a bus at 15.8 km/h with 0.8 s between road users.
The close pass involved a car at 44.4 km/h with 1.9 s between road users.

For adults hit by a car front, Rosén & Sander 2009 gives death risk of 14.5% at 57.0 km/h, 5.7% at 45.5 km/h, 2.3% at 34.8 km/h, 0.4% at 15.8 km/h and 1.9% at 44.4 km/h. Our youngest pupils would face about twice the adult chance of death if hit at those speeds.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, based on 90 pedestrians and 16 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 26.7 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice at 1.3x the true count in drone tests.
63.2% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, from 12 gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 73.9 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety works at Bridge Street crossing

We write from the school beside Bridge Street crossing. Crossing Watch measured the crossing for 25.8 minutes and recorded 32 crossings and 15 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 47.4 km/h.

There was 1 serious near-miss, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 1 close pass, defined as 1.5 to 3.0 s apart. The serious near-miss involved a bus at 46.0 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s. The close pass involved a bus at 22.2 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 1.7 s.

For adults hit by a car front, Rosén & Sander 2009 estimates the death risk at 46.0 km/h as 5.9% and at 22.2 km/h as 0.4%. A child hit in that worst encounter would have had a 12% chance of dying. At a 20.0 km/h limit the estimated impact speed for the worst case would be 20.0 km/h with 0.6% adult death risk, and for the second case 2.5 km/h with 0.1% adult death risk.

Engineering notes from the video: PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, scaled from 25.8 minutes of video, while a formal check counts the full peak hour. 55.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 4 gaps of 6 s or more, 2 of them 12 s or more and longest 86.2 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request a raised zebra crossing on a speed table with 20 km/h zone signs and markings at this location. We will share the full video and data on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Road Authority Officer,

We write about the Market Street crossing outside our school. Nearly all drivers were exceeding the posted speed limit through the school zone. Crossing Watch video analysis (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) measured 6 pedestrian crossings and 31 moving vehicles in 5.1 minutes (306.0 s).

In that period 6 of 6 crossings (1 in 1) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 2 of 6 (1 in 3) within 1.5 s. The most severe serious near-miss left 1.2 s between the person and a car travelling at 44.6 km/h, with an estimated adult fatality risk of 5.3% if hit by a car front (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+).

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Hill View Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the Hill View Road crossing outside our school. Crossing Watch analysis of 25.9 minutes of video (1554.0 s) recorded 40 crossings and 22 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 36.3 km/h. The closest of these passes was in fact a collision. In that period there were 2 serious near-misses and 1 close pass. A serious near-miss is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and a close pass as 1.5-3.0 s apart.

The most severe serious near-miss involved a van at 33.4 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.9 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 2.0% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared to 0.6% at 19.9 km/h if the 20 km/h limit had applied.

A second serious near-miss involved a bus at 29.5 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 1.4%, compared to 0.6% at 20.0 km/h if the 20 km/h limit had applied.

A close pass involved a bus at 13.1 km/h with a post-encroachment time of 2.4 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.0%, compared to 0.0% at 0.0 km/h if the 20 km/h limit had applied.

In total, 0 crossings had the person first, 3 had the vehicle first and 0 had both at once.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 93 pedestrians and 51 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 25.9 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice at 1.3x the true count in the drone test. About 55.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 1 gap of 6 s or more and 1 of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 86.6 s; the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce speeds and give priority to pedestrians.

We are willing to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
Approved by The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir / Madam,

I write for the school at Lake View Road crossing about pedestrian risk observed on video.

During 43.9 minutes of video, 23 crossings and 13 vehicles were recorded, with 85th percentile speed 50.7 km/h. 2 of 23 crossings (1 in 12) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person; 2 of 23 (1 in 12) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical: 1.1-28.0% and 1.1-28.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson); 0.2-7.2 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). By definition, serious means pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart.

1 serious near-miss involved a van at 50.4 km/h with 1.4 s between the person and the vehicle.
Another serious near-miss involved a van at 22.8 km/h with 0.7 s between the person and the vehicle. Almost all of the people crossing were young pupils from our school.
For adults hit by a car front (Rosen & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), estimated death risk if hit was 8.6% for the van at 50.4 km/h.
For adults hit by a car front on the same basis, estimated death risk if hit was 0.8% for the van at 22.8 km/h.
At a 20 km/h limit, impact was modelled as 0.0 km/h with 0.0% death risk for the case at 50.4 km/h.
At a 20 km/h limit, impact was modelled as 20.0 km/h with 0.6% death risk for the case at 22.8 km/h.
PV2 was 0.0 x 10^8 from 31 pedestrians and 18 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 43.9 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour.
86.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, noting the first and last are cut short by the video.

I request provision of a raised zebra crossing at Lake View Road crossing.
I offer to share the video for review on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning the Market Street crossing outside our school. Crossing Watch recorded 11.6 minutes of video covering 6 pedestrian crossings and 13 moving vehicles. The recording lasted 11.6 minutes and included 6 crossings and 13 vehicles over 5 gaps. The 85th percentile speed was 29.7 km/h.

Headline results were 3 of 6 crossings (1 in 2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s of the person and 2 of 6 (1 in 3) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 11.8-88.2% and 4.3-77.7% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart; close pass is 1.5-3.0 s.

The worst near-misses were as follows. One serious near-miss had a PET of 0.3 s with a car at 30.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 1.5% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), which would be 0.6% at impact of 20.0 km/h with a 20 km/h limit.

A second serious near-miss had a PET of 1.3 s with a car at 14.7 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.4%, which would remain 0.4% at impact of 14.7 km/h with a 20 km/h limit.

A close pass had a PET of 2.2 s with a car at 26.1 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front the death risk data shows 0.0% at that speed, and 0.0% at impact of 0.0 km/h with a 20 km/h limit.

Engineering context is limited: PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 11.6 minutes with 6 pedestrian crossings and 13 moving vehicles. 52.8% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 5 gaps and 0 of them 12 s or more and longest 9.8 s, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video. UK Traffic Signs Manual ch. 6 (13.5.2) notes 4-6 s is an acceptable gap at urban speeds and other groups, such as children, may need 10-12 s or longer.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone with signs at this location.

We can share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

Re: Safety improvement at Station Road crossing

We are writing to request safety improvements at the Station Road crossing outside our school.

Crossing Watch measurements cover 9.0 minutes (540.0 s) of video. In that time 4 pedestrian crossings and 18 moving vehicles were counted, with an 85th percentile speed of 34.2 km/h. Mrs. Leela Fernandes, who drives the morning bus, caused the worst of these events.

During the recording there were 3 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 1 close pass (1.5-3.0 s). For gaps, 77.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 5 gaps, 3 of them 12 s or more, longest 37.8 s (the first and last are cut short by the video). PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 9.0 minutes, so those rates are not used here.

The worst cases were:
One serious near-miss involved a van at 33.6 km/h with a separation of 0.2 s, with an adult death risk if hit of 2.0% (0.6% at 20.0 km/h).
Another serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 31.5 km/h with a separation of 0.5 s, with an adult death risk if hit of 1.7% (0.6% at 20.0 km/h).
A third serious near-miss involved a car at 13.7 km/h with a separation of 0.2 s, with an adult death risk if hit of 0.3%.
There was also 1 close pass by a car at 33.9 km/h with a separation of 2.1 s. Death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.
In 1 case the person was first and in 3 cases the vehicle was first, with 0 cases of both at once.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide protected priority for pedestrians.

We would be happy to share the video and SAM tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for raised zebra crossing at Lantern Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write as the school using Lantern Road crossing. A 36.0 minute video (2160.0 s) recorded 17 crossings and 30 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 55.3 km/h. 5 gaps were cut short by the start or end of the video.

Of the 17 crossings, 6 of 17 (1 in 2.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 5 of 17 (1 in 3.4) within 1.5 s. The exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 14.2-61.7% and 10.3-56.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 2.2-13.1 and 1.6-11.7 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

There were 5 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 1 close pass (1.5-3.0 s).

The most severe serious near-miss had a time gap of 1.0 s between the person and a bus travelling at 47.9 km/h, with an adult death risk of 7.0% if hit by a car front (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+).

A second serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.9 s with a car travelling at 47.7 km/h, with an adult death risk of 6.9% if hit.

A third serious near-miss had a time gap of 1.0 s with a car travelling at 28.5 km/h, with an adult death risk of 1.3% if hit.

A fourth serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.4 s with an auto-rickshaw travelling at 23.5 km/h, with an adult death risk of 0.8% if hit.

A fifth serious near-miss had a time gap of 0.3 s with a car travelling at 19.1 km/h, with an adult death risk of 0.6% if hit.

At a 20 km/h limit the estimated impact speeds and adult death risks for these 5 events would be 0.0 km/h and 0.0%, 0.0 km/h and 0.0%, 20.0 km/h and 0.6%, 20.0 km/h and 0.6%, and 19.1 km/h and 0.6% respectively.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 (28 pedestrians and 50 moving vehicles an hour, scaled from 36 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count 1.3x the true count). 75.3% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 5 such gaps and 2 of them 12 s or more and longest 82.0 s, noting the first and last are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with 20 km/h approach signs at this location to reduce speeds and provide priority.

We are willing to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

We write about the Ring Road crossing outside our school and request a raised zebra crossing.

Measurements from video of the crossing, made by Crossing Watch with SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time, covered 33.8 minutes, 2028.0 s, with 29 crossings and 6 vehicles recorded.

The 85th percentile speed was 19.8 km/h. In the near-miss with a time gap of 0.9 s, the motorcycle reached the spot after the pedestrian. There were 2 gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, 1 of them 12 s or more, with longest gap 86.4 s. In total 77.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more.

There was 1 serious near-miss and 0 close passes. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass as 1.5 to 3.0 s. In the serious case the vehicle arrived first in 1 case.

The worst serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 15.4 km/h. The pedestrian and the motorcycle were on the same spot 0.9 s apart. For an adult hit by a car front at that impact speed the death risk is 0.4% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts. At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 15.4 km/h with death risk 0.4% for an adult hit by a car front.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 51 pedestrians and 11 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 33.8 minutes of video. IRC:103-2012 cl. 6.7.4.1.2 notes a controlled crossing may be warranted above 1 x 10^8 on an undivided road and 2 x 10^8 on a divided road.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location and we offer to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully
The Principal
